books.why_zh: 在美国自身极化的当下，读一部把「两个美国」写成一确二真的小说——现实已经在分叉，小说只是把它显影。
books.why_en: In a moment of American fracturing, a novel that writes "two Americas" as one-true-two — reality is already forking; fiction only develops the film.

background.zh: 曼德尔 2026 年的第七部长篇，也是她最政治化的作品。2031 年一场政变后美国分崩离析为互战的共和国、城邦与民兵地盘（A 面，混乱）；同书并置一个从未分裂、却收缩为铁腕监控国家的「美利坚合众国」（B 面，极权）。两个美国由一场洛杉矶派对事故与一幅 1968 年的画作《天鹅潜水》（Swan Dive）相连。A 面的混乱与 B 面的秩序互为「国家的反生活」，也是作者对「半数选民在基本事实上都不再一致」的当下焦虑的直接投影。曼德尔自称「最政治、最酷儿、最好的小说」。
background.en: Mandel's seventh novel and her most openly political. After a 2031 coup the U.S. splinters into warring republics/city-states and militia zones (A-Side, chaos); a parallel America never fragments but constricts into a surveillance state run by the "Service" (B-Side). The two are bridged by a party accident and a 1968 painting, "Swan Dive." Chaos and totalitarianism function as a "dark twinship" — the counterlife of the state — mirroring Mandel's anxiety that "half the electorate disagrees on basic reality." She calls it "my most political work, my most queer work, I think it's my best novel."

plot_acts.zh: 2031 年春——美国政变崩解后的「第一个春天」。国际维和部队撤离洛杉矶，宵禁随《萨克拉门托协定》解除，加州共和国成立。48 岁的阿里·韦克刚出狱（18 年刑期，雇凶杀害表兄安东）。她与室友格洛丽亚穿过棚户区、红十字帐篷与炸弹嗅探犬去银湖参加卡里姆·法耶德的派对。派对上「出了毛病」：塞拉亚的第二个版本（穿便装的困惑女人）现身又逃入夜色；自称尼科的「第二个格洛丽亚」闯入厨房；主人卡里姆在一间没有外门的厨房里凭空消失。格洛丽亚取下画作《天鹅潜水》带画赴欧洲（她怀着卡里姆的孩子）。事后有人对阿里说：「我想，那场派对也是一扇门。」
plot_acts.en: In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, peacekeepers withdraw from LA, the curfew is lifted (Sacramento Accord), the Republic of California is declared. Ari Waker, 48, is newly released after 18 years for hiring a hit on her cousin. She walks with roommate Gloria to Kareem Fayed's Silverlake party past tent cities and bomb-sniffing dogs. At the flower-filled party "there's something wrong": a second, casually dressed Saraya appears and flees; a woman entering the kitchen; the host Kareem vanishes from a doorless kitchen. Gloria takes the painting and flees to Europe, pregnant. "I think the party was also a door."
plot_acts.sources: npr.org · wsj.com · thesaturdaypaper.com.au · lithub.com

plot_acts.zh: 阿里在崩解的 A 面世界漂泊求生：洛杉矶街头当洗碗工/零售店员；东迁俄亥俄共和国，为饯行组织做杂役、替民兵头目爱德华多跟踪尼科；与曾是芭蕾舞者的军火商费利克斯结伴南下得克萨斯，再逃往欧洲（巴黎圆顶孤城、希腊军火商据点）。她后来甩掉费利克斯，与雇佣兵比尔·索里亚诺结成交易式联盟，最终化名巴黎艺术藏家「阿里·索里亚诺」。她天生的预感（clairvoyance）时灵时不灵。核心台词：「若没有人见证，你的过去就开始像虚构。」
plot_acts.en: Ari drifts through the broken A-Side world: dishwashing/retail in LA, militia work in the Ohio Republic (surveilling Nico for Eduardo), a partnership with Felix (a former ballet dancer turned gunrunner), flight through Texas to Europe (domed Paris, a Greek militia hangout), a transactional alliance with mercenary Bill Soriano, and finally a life as Paris art collector "Ari Soriano." Her premonitions are unreliable. Motto-line: "If you don't have a witness, your past starts to feel fictional."
plot_acts.sources: npr.org · bostonglobe.com · brooklynrail.org · theguardian.com

plot_acts.zh: B 面：合众国没有崩解，却成了极权国家——「Service」（内部安全局）当街掳人，劳动营供「批评政府者」改造；投票不再必需，总统之位预定由他儿子接任。UCLA 四名物理学家——尼科·李、丈夫卡里姆·法耶德、塞拉亚·德·桑托斯与同事莱恩——深夜秘密做传送实验：先用《天鹅潜水》试机（完美传送），随后卡里姆踏上平台，被复制成两个——B 面出现两个卡里姆，均被 Service 羁押；同时 A 面派对上的卡里姆在厨房消失。阿里的 B 面对应体是资深探员伊巴里·韦克：公开职业是城市规划讲师；鼻梁上一副银胶带修补的眼镜可骗过人脸识别；她自称「我一生都带着一点点直觉」。她用假名「大卫·格里森」（《歌者之枪》旧角色）救出 A 面卡里姆。
plot_acts.en: B-Side America stayed whole — and constricted: the "Service" yanks people into unmarked cars, labor camps reform critics, voting is no longer required. Four UCLA physicists (Nico Li, her husband Kareem Fayed, Saraya de Santos, colleague Len) secretly run a teleportation experiment; "Swan Dive" transmits perfectly, then Kareem steps on the platform and is duplicated — two Kareems, both detained. Ari's parallel is Ibari Waker, senior Service detective whose cover is urban-planning professor; her silver-taped glasses defeat facial recognition. She frees the A-side Kareem under the alias "David Grissom" (a Singer's Gun character).
plot_acts.sources: npr.org · wired.com (excerpt) · thesaturdaypaper.com.au

plot_acts.zh: 故事跨越数十年。巴黎在对世界其余部分关闭的圆顶内成为相对安稳的孤岛（约 2065 年前后）。格洛丽亚是不尽责的母亲；尼科成为塞巴斯蒂安（格洛丽亚与 A 面卡里姆之子）的代理母亲；《天鹅潜水》经手多人。塞巴斯蒂安 20 岁决定把画从年迈藏家阿里·索里亚诺处「偷回」，作为给尼科的生日礼物；阿里在巴黎文森森林追逐画作时被劫匪重创。B 面：获释的卡里姆患癌临终，成年的萨米尔（月面殖民地建筑师）与马洛（传送物理学家、患有「时间线损坏」式的复杂 PTSD）守于床边；另一个卡里姆翻窗而入与他道别。动身退休的伊巴里（79 岁）行使「火化权」销毁追踪编码、下载国家机密档案交给抵抗组织，随后独自走进太平洋。
plot_acts.en: The novel arcs across decades into a domed-Paris refuge (circa 2065) sealed off from the broken world. Gloria is a neglectful mother; Nico is a surrogate mother to Sebastian (Gloria's son by the party Kareem). Sebastian, at 20, decides to steal "Swan Dive" back from elderly collector Ari Soriano as a birthday present for Nico; Ari is badly hurt chasing him through the Bois de Vincennes. B-Side: the freed Kareem dies of cancer with grown Samir (architect on the lunar colony) and Marlowe (a transport physicist wracked by complex PTSD — "timeline corruption") at his bedside; the other Kareem climbs in a window to say goodbye. Retiring Ibari (79) uses her "right of incineration," destroys her trackers, copies the State's files to the Resistance, then walks into the Pacific surf.
plot_acts.sources: ursummary.com ◐ · brooklynrail.org · thesaturdaypaper.com.au · thebcreview.ca

plot_acts.zh: 尾声不以乌托邦收束，而以「一丝希望的微光」收束：艺术的长寿与「短暂即甜蜜」互为支撑；「如果世上没有见证者，你的过去就开始像虚构」一语回收。曼德尔强调这是「希望之书」，是疫情后纽约那个奇迹般盛夏的「desperate joy」所驱动。
plot_acts.en: The ending declines utopia for "a little glimmer of hope": art outliving makers and countries is the governing theme; "temporary brings its own kind of sweetness" recurs. Mandel insists this is a hopeful book born of the "desperate joy" of New York's magical pandemic-era summer.
plot_acts.sources: defector.com · therumpus.net · elle.com

narrative.zh: 全书三部分——A-Side（A 面/混乱宇宙）、B-Side（B 面/极权宇宙）、Swan Dive（《天鹅潜水》：近卷末的短章，交代画作 1968 年在纽约公寓的缘起）。整体第三人称叙述，部分段落转为现在时；章节内嵌标题小节（如「The Birthday Present」「True Diligence」）；含审讯转录稿——其中一段是「只听一方」的独角转录，书评人指为炫技。双镜结构：A/B 两面的对应人物互为「反生活」，以跨世界重复的句子与意象缝合全书（「我想跳进海里，一路游过那片蓝」「真正的勤奋=追随不可能之路」「PTSD 是时间线损坏」）。机制几乎不给解释——可穿点疑似为「同时存在于两个宇宙的物体」（画作），而书内尼科自嘲「我觉得那幅画是个障眼法」。
narrative.en: Three parts — A-Side, B-Side, and a late, short "Swan Dive" section on the painting's 1968 New York origins. Third person throughout (present tense in stretches); embedded titled micro-chapters; an interrogation transcript, plus a famously one-sided "transcript" chapter that critics call showy. The doubled worlds braid via mirror-selves and repeated lines/images. The physics is deliberately unexplained — "a notion that objects might be where parallel universes converge" — undercut in-text by Nico: "I think the painting's a red herring."

quotes.orig: An idea that I've been fascinated with for a long time is this notion of the counterlife, the life you didn't live.
quotes.trans_zh: 「反生活」（counterlife）这个念头我着迷已久——那些你未曾活过的生活。
quotes.source: irishtimes.com 2026-09-12
quotes.trans_en: "Counterlife" — the life you did not live — is a notion that has fascinated me for a long time.

quotes.orig: It's interesting to think about the counterlife of the individual, but it's also interesting to think about the counterlife of the state.
quotes.trans_zh: 想象个体的反生活很有意思，但想想「国家的反生活」也耐人寻味。
quotes.source: lithub.com (Jane Ciabattari) 2026-09-15
quotes.trans_en: It's interesting to think of the counterlife of the individual, but also of the counterlife of the state.

quotes.orig: I've never been particularly interested in disaster, but I am interested in its aftermath. There's hope in thinking about the world that follows catastrophic events.
quotes.trans_zh: 我对「灾难」本身从不特别感兴趣，我感兴趣的是灾难之后的事。想象大灾后的世界，其中是有希望的。
quotes.source: lithub.com
quotes.trans_en: I've never been much interested in disaster itself — what interests me is its aftermath. There is hope in imagining the world that follows catastrophic events.

quotes.orig: Who will you be at the end of the world? I think of that as the book's central question.
quotes.trans_zh: 「世界落幕时你会成为怎样的人？」——我认为这是全书的核心之问。
quotes.source: irishtimes.com
quotes.trans_en: "Who will you be at the end of the world?" — that I take to be the book's central question.

quotes.orig: That feeling of desperate joy at the end of the world, that was something I was really trying to capture… There is a lot of joy even in these incredibly compromised times.
quotes.trans_zh: 「世界尽头的绝望之乐」正是我想抓住的……哪怕在如此千疮百孔的时代，也仍有大量快乐。
quotes.trans_en: That desperate joy at the end of the world is what I was trying to capture… even in these deeply compromised times there is a great deal of joy.

quotes.orig: The collapse of consensual reality. When you get to a situation where half the electorate disagrees on basic reality… I don't know how you come back from that.
quotes.trans_zh: 共识性现实的坍塌。当半数选民连最基本的事实都达不成一致……我不知道这该怎么弥合。
quotes.source: theguardian.com 2026-09-13
quotes.trans_en: The collapse of consensual reality. Once half the electorate can't agree on basic facts… I don't know how you come back from that.

intent.reception_good_zh: Kirkus——「自《大站十一》以来最好的作品……把平行时间线的概念天才地接上政治主题」；Booklist、Library Journal 星评；Publishers Weekly ★「tour de force」。NPR 的 Corrigan 说「派对值得等待」；New Yorker 的 Waldman 自称「一口读完」；Boston Globe「曼德尔最好的状态」；Saturday Paper「精彩、完全笃定」。
intent.reception_good_en: Kirkus — "best since Station Eleven… brilliantly ties parallel timelines to a political theme"; Booklist & Library Journal starred; PW ★ "tour de force." NPR's Corrigan: the party "is worth the wait"; The New Yorker's Waldman "gulped it down"; Boston Globe: "Mandel at her best."
intent.reception_bad_zh: 反面/保留：Irish Examiner ——情节「unwieldy（笨重）」、结尾「陷入混乱」；Goodreads 1.5★ 博客则骂前提拉仲；BookAndFilmGlobe「圆满收束但非解决」；New Yorker 亦点出主角群「each seem to represent a different ethnic group」的危险——近乎零风险的讨好式演员名单。文学评论（Literary Review of Canada, 2026-10）正文未取到（○）。
intent.reception_bad_en: Dissent: Irish Examiner calls the plot "unwieldy" and the climax "descends into confusion"; a 1.5★ Goodreads blog resents stretched premises; BookAndFilmGlobe: "satisfying closure but not resolution." The New Yorker flags the "attractive prodigies" who "each seem to represent a different ethnic group." Literary Review of Canada, 2026-10 unretrieved (○).
intent.syn_zh: 作者明确把书写成「关于余波而非灾难」的希望之书，同时它是警世书：监控调性之外，「当半国选民不信基本事实」才是她笔下两个世界共同的原初创伤。主流书评盛赞居多；质疑集中在结构炫技与中段巴黎的拖沓。
intent.syn_en: Mandel frames the book as about aftermaths, not disasters, while warning that fractured consensus reality is the root trauma of both worlds. Mainstream reception is largely rapturous (Kirkus: "best since Station Eleven"), with dissent on pacing and the showy transcripts.
intent.sources: irishtimes.com · theguardian.com · lithub.com · elle.com · newyorker.com · npr.org · wsj.com

craft.zh: 画作作纽带——一幅《天鹅潜水》串起 A/B 两面与十余年幕：艺术是「最古老的时间旅行器」，延续《大站十一》的漫画即契约母题。
craft.en: The painting as thread — "Swan Dive" ties A/B sides across decades; art is "the oldest time machine," continuing Station Eleven's comics-as-covenant motif.

craft.zh: A/B=唱片 AB 面——双面结构取黑胶语义，「无须对称」；B 面机械的和谐反写 A 面随机的枪火。
craft.en: A/B updates an LP's sides — "you don't demand symmetry"; B-side's mechanical harmony inverts A-side's random fire.

craft.zh: 重复句缝合世界——跨世界重复的句子制造「既视感的惊悚」（"I want to dive into the ocean and keep swimming through the blue"; "True diligence means following the improbable path"）。
craft.en: Repeated sentences across worlds create déjà-vu dread, reading the two worlds as one coin.

craft.zh: 零科学软科幻——机制从不解释：「如果书里有时间机器，我不会告诉你怎么运作」，重点在人。
craft.en: "If there's a time machine in my book, I'm not going to tell you how it works" — the physics stays unexplainable.

craft.zh: PTSD=时间线损坏——用科幻概念映射日常心理损伤，是全书的微缩模型。
craft.en: "PTSD is timeline corruption" compresses the novel's theme into an aphorism.

craft.zh: 酷儿与照护——与早期作品相比，「做母亲」上升为核心情感（女儿 2015 年出生后她自认才懂某些细微差别）；阿里的双性恋被无戏剧化地正面写出。
craft.en: Parenthood became a core emotional register after her daughter's 2015 birth; Ari's bisexuality is stated without drama.

motifs.name_en: party as door / doorway and faction
motifs.evid_zh: 全书钥匙母题：派对既是字面的门（无外门的厨房），也是宇宙论的门（物体是平行世界相交之处）；「party」兼指社交聚会与政治党派——一个词承载两重灾难（国家碎裂 vs 极权收束）。开场的洛杉矶夜景里，「一身银裙、褶如锡箔」的女子在派对上出现为一重分裂的预兆。
motifs.evid_en: The book's hinge-motif: the party is a literal door (the kitchen with no door) and a cosmological one (objects as the convergences of parallel universes); "party" doubles as social gathering and political faction — one word, two collapses.
motifs.orig: I think the party was also a door.

motifs.name_zh: 天鹅潜水 · 画作纽带
motifs.name_en: Swan Dive — the painting as thread
motifs.evid_zh: 跨作品之物：《天鹅潜水》早在《玻璃旅馆》（2019）出场，在此成为情节枢纽——既是私人物品史，也印证「艺术比承载它的人与国更长寿」；作者称艺术是「最古老的时间旅行器」，延续《大站十一》的漫画即契约母题（结构无损层的 cross-text object）。
motifs.evid_en: A cross-book object: "Swan Dive" first appeared in The Glass Hotel (2019) and is central here — a micro-history of art outliving people and nations, the "oldest time machine," continuing Station Eleven's art-as-covenant motif.
motifs.orig: The painting, "Swan Dive," first appeared in The Glass Hotel (2019), and is central to the plot here.

motifs.name_en: jacaranda — beauty on its own calendar
motifs.evid_zh: 开篇第一句的景象母题：被战争、宵禁与维和部队撤军标记的「第一个春天」，由一棵南美外来树的气味打开——灾难下的美不来自国家，而来自仍按时开花的东西。
motifs.evid_en: The opening-image motif: the "first spring" after the collapse is opened by a smell, not by the state — a South American import that keeps to its own calendar.
motifs.orig: In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace.

motifs.name_zh: 国家的反生活 · 两版美国
motifs.name_en: counterlife of the state — two versions of the country
motifs.evid_zh: 比喻由人滑向国家：不只个人有分身的「反生活」，国家也有——一个世界「碎裂成一片狼藉」，另一个「收缩成一只拳头」；无序的散开与压抑的收束，两极同源。
motifs.evid_en: The simile slides from persons to the country: one world "fractured into disarray," the other "closed like a fist" — a civilization's dystopia and a police state's, shaped by the same fear.
motifs.orig: There was a world where my homeland had fractured into disarray, and another where my homeland had closed like a fist.

motifs.name_zh: 和谐不惜代价 · 监控即服务
motifs.name_en: harmony at any cost — surveillance as Service
motifs.evid_zh: B 面极权的排比宣言：「混乱的对立面是和谐；和平靠监控达成；服务局即国家的监控部门；不惜代价的和谐」。把监控委婉命名为「Service」，秩序被定义为混乱的对立面——而非混沌与自由。
motifs.evid_en: The B-side manifesto in tetracolon: order as the opposite of disorder, not of chaos and freedom — surveillance rebranded as "Service," harmony at any cost.
motifs.orig: The opposite of disorder is harmony. Peace is achieved through surveillance. Service is the surveillance department of the State. Harmony at any cost.

motifs.name_zh: 见证公信 · 无证即虚构
motifs.name_en: witness — without a witness, the past turns fictional
motifs.evid_zh: 全书母题最凝缩的一句（也是本仓「witness-aesthetics」术语的源头）：没有见证者，记忆就失去公信力——个人如此，国家亦然，史学即见证。
motifs.evid_en: The tersest statement of the book's core concern: without a witness the past loses all standing — true of persons, true of countries. History is testimony, or it is fiction.
motifs.orig: If you don't have a witness, your past starts to feel fictional.

excerpts.orig: In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace.
excerpts.trans_zh: 在美国崩塌之后的第一个春天，蓝花楹的盛放于阿里而言，如同恩典。
excerpts.trans_en: In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace.
excerpts.note_zh: 「白莲木/蓝花楹」点燃的是春天——南美洲原生、被引进洛杉矶的树，花在干热的五月盛放成片紫云。一个被战争、宵禁与维和部队撤军标记的「第一个春天」，却由这棵外来树的气味打开：灾难之下的美，不来自宏大的国家，而来自仍按时开花的东西。
excerpts.note_en: The jacaranda — a South American native imported into Los Angeles — erupts in purple in the dry May heat. The "first spring" after the collapse is opened by a smell, not by the state: beauty that keeps to its own calendar. Note the past-simple precision — one clause, no flourish — pure Mandel.

excerpts.orig: I think the party was also a door. / There's something wrong with the party. / There were extra people.
excerpts.trans_zh: 我想，那场派对也是一扇门。/ 派对上出了毛病。/ 那里有额外的人。
excerpts.trans_en: I think the party was also a door. / There's something wrong with the party. / There were extra people.
excerpts.note_zh: 全书的钥匙句：「门」既是字面的（无外门的厨房），也是宇宙论的（物体是平行宇宙相交之处）。「有额外的人」——party 在这里带着双重语义：既指派对，也指政治党派。一个词承担两重灾难。
excerpts.note_en: The hinge-line of the whole book: "door" is literal (the kitchen with no door) and cosmological (objects as the convergence of parallel universes). And "party" doubles: a social party and a political party — one word, two collapses.

excerpts.orig: The opposite of disorder is harmony. Peace is achieved through surveillance. Service is the surveillance department of the State. Harmony at any cost.
excerpts.trans_zh: 混乱的对立面是和谐；和平靠监控达成；服务局即国家的监控部门；不惜一切代价的和谐。
excerpts.trans_en: The opposite of disorder is harmony. Peace is achieved through surveillance. Service is the surveillance department of the State. Harmony at any cost.
excerpts.note_zh: 极权宣言式的排比。「Service」（服务局）一词的官僚委婉：把监控称作「为维持和谐服务」。四个短句，一句比一句紧，最后落到「Harmony at any cost」——不惜代价的和谐，即不择手段。
excerpts.note_en: A manifesto in tetracolon — each clause tightening toward "Harmony at any cost." The bureaucratic euphemism at work: surveillance rebranded as "Service"; order as the opposite of disorder, not of chaos and freedom.

excerpts.orig: Strange to think there weren't just two versions of me, and two versions of Kareem and Nico and possibly everyone else, but two versions of our country. There was a world where my homeland had fractured into disarray, and another where my homeland had closed like a fist.
excerpts.trans_zh: 奇怪的是，不只是我有两个版本，卡里姆、尼科乃至每个人都可能有两个版本——不，是我们国家有两个版本：一个世界里故土碎裂成一片狼藉，另一个世界里故土收缩成一只拳头。
excerpts.trans_en: Strange to think there weren't just two versions of me, and two versions of Kareem and Nico and possibly everyone else, but two versions of our country. There was a world where my homeland had fractured into disarray, and another where my homeland had closed like a fist.
excerpts.note_zh: 「国家的反生活」的点题之笔：比喻由人滑向国家——「碎裂成一片狼藉」与「收缩成一只拳头」。「fractured / closed like a fist」：无序的散开与压抑的收束，两极同源。
excerpts.note_en: The motif-line of the "counterlife of the state": the simile slides from persons (two versions of me) to the country. "Fractured into disarray" vs "closed like a fist" — a civilization's dystopia and a police state's, equally shaped by the same fear.

excerpts.orig: I have spent my whole life pulling pins on grenades… I want extremity. I want annihilation. I want to blow up my life and remake it, but how many times do you get to do that?
excerpts.trans_zh: 我这一辈子都在拔手榴弹的保险栓……我想要极端，想要湮灭，想炸掉我的人生重新来过——可这种事，人能有几次？
excerpts.trans_en: I have spent my whole life pulling pins on grenades… I want extremity. I want annihilation. I want to blow up my life and remake it, but how many times do you get to do that?
excerpts.note_zh: 伊巴里（B 面探员）的自白：把人生过成反复拔保险栓。「blow up my life and remake it」——「blow up」兼有引爆与重塑两义。反生活视角下，毁灭即重造。
excerpts.note_en: Ibari's confession: a life lived as pulling pins. "Blow up" is wonderfully ambiguous — detonate and reimagine at once. Under the counterlife lens, destruction is the price of remaking.

excerpts.orig: If you don't have a witness, your past starts to feel fictional.
excerpts.trans_zh: 若是没有人见证，你的过去就开始变得像虚构。
excerpts.trans_en: If you don't have a witness, your past starts to feel fictional.
excerpts.note_zh: 全书母题最凝缩的一句（亦是本板块术语架 witness-aesthetics 的源头）：没有见证者，记忆就失去公信力。个人如此，国家亦然——史学即见证。
excerpts.note_en: The tersest statement of the book's core concern and the seed of this domain's "witness-aesthetics" term: without a witness the past loses all standing — true of persons, true of countries. History is testimony, or it is fiction.

deep_read.zh: 把 A/B 两面当作「同一焦虑的两种结局」来读，而非平行世界解谜：逐句捕捉跨面的镜像句与镜像人物（Ari/Ibari、格洛丽亚/尼科、双卡里姆、萨米尔/马洛、费利克斯/爱德华多）。
deep_read.en: Read A/B as twin outcomes of one anxiety, tracking mirror-sentences and mirror-selves (Ari/Ibari, Gloria/Nico, the two Kareems, Samir/Marlowe) rather than solving the portal.

deep_read.zh: 逐一到路追踪《天鹅潜水》的每一次转手（派对墙→格洛丽亚→塞巴斯蒂安→尼科→伊巴里）：这是一部私人物品史，也印证「艺术比承载它的人与国更长寿」的主题。
deep_read.en: Map every hand-off of "Swan Dive" — a micro-history of art outliving people and nations, Mandel's central thesis.

deep_read.zh: 注意文体异色：审讯转录、独角转录、1968 年画作前史。作者坦承在「神秘但不令人抓狂地困惑」上走钢丝；The Leftovers（剧集）提供氛围参照。
deep_read.en: Watch the formal oddities (interrogation/one-sided transcripts, the 1968 origin chapter) against her stated tightrope — "mysterious, but not maddeningly confusing" — with The Leftovers as tonal precedent.

deep_read.zh: 预兆的「失灵」是自嘲的传记性投射（「我绝对无法预测大流行病」）——别把超自然当答案，答案在「见证」与照护里。
deep_read.en: Treat Ari's premonitions as wry self-portrait ("I absolutely cannot predict pandemics") — the answer is witness and care, not psi.

background.zh: 瓦尔加《亚当斯贝格探案》第 11 卷，2026 年 4 月 8 日由 Flammarion 出版（528 页）。书名 « Une unique lueur »（一束唯一的光）取自内瓦尔《El Desdichado》名句，与全书的核心谜面直接挂钩。注意：2026 年另有同名异书（另一作者的同名小说），须以 Flammarion 本与 Adamsberg 线索区隔。此前的二手梗概（Fraixen 老翁、斯宾诺莎时代、1980 档案、自杀调查局）经检索均未见于任何权威源——判为证伪锚点，一律不录入；确证在书内的元素：街头「完美」女尸（银莲花、金哨）、内瓦尔《El Desdichado》、白考尔/鲍嘉形象、六年前的悬案翻查、记忆-复诵主题，以及全书多语种页注。
background.en: Adamsberg #11, published by Flammarion on 8 April 2026 (528 pp). The title "Une unique lueur" — one single glimmer — is taken from Nerval's El Desdichado and keys the whole enigma. Caution: another same-titled novel by a different author also appeared in 2026; distinguish by the Flammarion imprint and the Adamsberg series. Earlier secondhand plot anchors (Fraixen, the Spinoza era, 1980 archives, a suicide-investigations bureau) were falsified by search — none appear in any authoritative source, so they are not recorded. Confirmed in-book elements: the "perfect" corpse (anemones, golden whistle), Nerval's El Desdichado, the Bacall/Bogart imagery, re-opening of a six-year-old case, the memory-repetition theme, and the book's multi-language page notes.
background.conf: ✓ 出版信息；情节锚点甄别后 ✓/◐
background.sources: fr.wikipedia (Flammarion) · dequoilire · lemondedupolar · éditeur 目录

plot_acts.zh: 巴黎街头发现一具被精心「造型」的年轻女性尸体：格纹套装、精致妆容、身旁银莲花、颈间金色哨子——谋杀被塑造成一场美学作品。亚当斯贝格（Adamsberg）直觉嗅到这不是普通的凶案，而是一种「图像生成」：凶手按某个文学/电影范本把受害者「酿」成偶像化身。
plot_acts.en: A young woman's body is found on a Paris street, meticulously "styled": skirt suit, precise make-up, anemones at her side, a golden whistle at her throat — murder staged as a work of art. Adamsberg senses this is not an ordinary killing but image-making: the killer is "composing" victims into icons according to a literary/film template.
plot_acts.conf: ◐ (概要；核心意象与公开评论一致)
plot_acts.sources: fr 媒体书评综合 · lemondedupolar · dequoilire

plot_acts.zh: 调查通向内瓦尔《El Desdichado》（「孤毁者、鳏夫、无可慰藉者」）——书名「一束唯一的光」正出自该诗；另一条线索是白考尔（Lauren Bacall）与鲍嘉（Bogart）的电影形象。凶手把女性「排演」进偶像崇拜的构图里：文学与电影不是线索，而是他的世界观本身。
plot_acts.en: The case converges on Nerval's El Desdichado ("the dark one, the widower, the disconsolate") — the novel's title is lifted from it — and on the Bacall/Bogart film iconography. The killer stages women inside an idolatrous composition: literature and film are not clues, they are his worldview.
plot_acts.sources: 公开评论确认 Nerval/El Desdichado/白考尔/鲍嘉为在场元素
plot_acts.sources_en: Public reviews confirm Nerval / El Desdichado / Bacall / Bogart as on-page elements

plot_acts.zh: 同一手法指向六年前一起不了了之的悬案。亚当斯贝格执意把两案并卷——「记忆-复诵」的母题（人物反复重述、行走、绕圈）成了解开谜题的关键。全书的页下注释多语种并置，呼应语言的边界与迷思的迁移。
plot_acts.en: The same method points back to a six-year-old cold case. Adamsberg insists on rejoining the two files — and the novel's memory-repetition motif (characters who repeat, walk, circle) becomes the key. Multi-language page notes mirror how words and delusions migrate across borders.
plot_acts.sources: 公开评论 · fr.wikipedia

narrative.zh: 延续 Adam 系列标志性的「直觉破案」：标靶式轻描淡写的人物速写、突然的闪回、以及让调查显得玄学的闲笔。叙事节奏在 vargas 式「预感」与冷硬现实探案之间摆动；书内引文与页注承担大量互文谜面（多语种）。
narrative.en: Classic Adamsberg intuition-led detection: shorthand character sketches, sudden flashbacks, throwaway lines that make detection look like divination. The narration swings between Vargas-style "hunch" and hard police procedure; quotations and (multi-language) page notes carry much of the intertext.

intent.reception_good_zh: 法语书评普遍侧重「标题取内瓦尔《El Desdichado》『一束唯一的光』」的互文设计；认为本作延续 Vargas 对直觉-理性的辩证，是代表性的 Adamsberg 长篇。
intent.reception_good_en: French reviews focus on the Nerval title-echo and welcome another trademark Adamsberg meditation on intuition vs. reason.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 个别读感：历来被诟病的「结局玄学化」在本作依旧；中段对记忆主题的复诵被认为略有自我重复。
intent.reception_bad_en: Recurring complaints persist: the finales feel quasi-mystical; the memory-repetition theme risks sounding self-referential.
intent.syn_zh: 作者把「美学化的暴力」摆成谜面本身——文学与影像不是装饰，而是凶手看世界的镜头。书名即答案的一半。
intent.syn_en: The novel makes aestheticized violence the enigma itself — literature and film aren't décor but the killer's lens. The title is half the answer.

excerpts.orig: «Je suis le ténébreux, — le veuf, — l'inconsolé.» (Nerval, «El Desdichado»)
excerpts.trans_zh: 「我乃幽冥者，——鳏夫，——无可慰藉者。」——书名及谜面的源文本。
excerpts.source: fr.wikipedia · 公开评论确认在书内被引用
excerpts.trans_en: "I am the dark one — the widower — the inconsolable one." (Gérard de Nerval, "El Desdichado")
excerpts.note_zh: 书名《Une unique lueur》（一束独光）正脱胎于这首诗。「ténébreux / veuf / inconsolé」三连呼，是法国浪漫主义最著名的一句——诗人以失星者自喻（「我的唯一的星已经熄灭」）。瓦尔加借这句诗把罪案谜面沉入法国文学传统的底色：一束光，在黑暗中辨认。
excerpts.note_en: The novel's title quotes this line from Nerval's great sonnet "El Desdichado" — "my one Star is dead." Three vocatives (dark one / widower / inconsolable) make it the most famous opening in French Romanticism. Vargas plants her murder-mystery inside that literary shadow: one glimmer, held up against the dark.
excerpts.source_en: fr.wikipedia · public reviews confirm it is quoted in the book

deep_read.zh: 把整部小说当作对《El Desdichado》的「一束光的注解」来读：留意每次对诗句的引用，都对应凶手布置图景的一次『取景』。
deep_read.en: Read the novel as an extended gloss on El Desdichado's "unique lueur": each quotation is a frame the killer has composed.

deep_read.zh: 追踪银莲花（anémone）与金哨的每一次出现——它们是物件间的坐标，Vargas 惯用「微小信物」串联直觉逻辑。
deep_read.en: Track the anemone and the golden whistle on every appearance — Vargas's small tokens that chain her intuitive logic.

books.why_zh: 当「光荣岁月」被供奉为集体记忆，谁有资格掀开它的阴影——小说与历史，法理与人情。
books.why_en: When the Glory Years are enshrined as collective memory, who is entitled to lift their shadow — fiction and history, law and feeling.

background.zh: 勒梅特「光荣岁月」（Les Années glorieuses）四部曲终章，2026-01-06 出版，512 页，真实 ISBN 9782702191477（旧卡 9782702189825/543pp 已更正）。背景设定在 1963–64 年的巴黎与乡村：长子让·佩尔格（Jean Pelletier）因在火灾中救出一名婴儿而成为国民英雄，被捧为「美丽的承诺」的化身；他的弟弟弗朗索瓦却开始怀疑——这个被全家供奉的英雄，正是连环杀害年轻女性的真凶。经济繁荣的「光辉三十年」遮蔽了道德的溃败：进步的神话与它庇护的罪长自同一根。
background.en: Finale of Lemaitre's Glorious Years quartet, published 2026-01-06, 512 pp, ISBN 9782702191477 (corrected from the wrong 9782702189825/543pp in the earlier card). Set in 1963–64 Paris and the countryside: eldest son Jean Pelletier, a national hero for saving a baby from a fire, becomes the incarnation of "beautiful promises"; his brother François begins to suspect the family's idol is the serial killer of young women. The boom of les Trente Glorieuses masks moral decay — the myth of progress and the crime it shelters grow from the same root.

plot_acts.zh: 巴黎 1963–64。让·佩尔格为救火中婴儿成为国家英雄——媒体造神、「美丽的承诺」全民共情。家中老猫约瑟夫（Joseph）是沉默的观察者。弟弟弗朗索瓦试笔的小说《美丽的承诺》（书名即来自这部「手稿」）把兄长写成连环杀人犯，而现实中蹊跷的失踪案接踵而至。
plot_acts.en: Paris 1963–64. Jean Pelletier becomes a national hero rescuing a baby from a fire — the press canonizes him, "beautiful promises" everywhere. The family cat Joseph is the silent witness. Brother François's manuscript-novel Les Belles Promesses (the real title) imagines the eldest as a serial murderer — then girls really start disappearing.
plot_acts.sources: surbooke · nyctalopes 长篇评论

plot_acts.zh: 弗朗索瓦的怀疑撞上家族的集体回避：母亲热纳维耶芙（Geneviève）持家、弟妹菲利普与科莱特各有城府，全家以「英雄崇拜」为铁律拒绝追问。次线：阿尔及利亚退伍兵曼努埃尔·拉莫斯（Manuel Ramos）的乡村悲剧——被解放的战争创伤与战后「进步」叙事在底层土地上的回响。
plot_acts.en: François's suspicion meets the family's collective refusal to ask: Geneviève keeps the house, siblings Philippe and Colette have agendas, and hero-worship is the rule. Subplot: Manuel Ramos, an Algeria veteran, carries the war's unresolved trauma into the postwar countryside.
plot_acts.sources: Médiapart · nyctalopes

plot_acts.zh: 英雄神话与罪行在同一家族体内对质。终局并不给出廉价的救赎：进步年代的账单由谁付？——「光荣岁月」的每一分荣耀都被标了价。
plot_acts.en: The hero-myth and the crime collide inside the same family. No cheap redemption: someone pays for every ounce of the Glory Years' glory.
plot_acts.sources: Médiapart 长评

narrative.zh: 勒梅特的典型声部：高速第三人称、冷峻的黑色幽默、家族史诗的大构架与小景深高密度切换。小说借「书内书」（François 的《美丽的承诺》手稿）制造叙述套盒：作者、角色与读者共享同一份猜疑。
narrative.en: Lemaitre's signature register: rapid third-person, bleak humour, the big family-epic frame cut with dense close-ups. The novel-within-the-novel (François's manuscript) creates a nesting of suspicion shared by author, character and reader.

intent.reception_good_zh: 法媒普遍称赞终章把四部曲收束到「家—历史—正义」三角，猫约瑟夫的设置被反复引用为全书最锋利的意象。
intent.reception_good_en: French media praise the quartet's convergence on family–history–justice; the cat Joseph is repeatedly cited as the sharpest image.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 部分评论认为乡村次线与巴黎主线两线并轨略迟，节奏在第三卷末处偏缓。
intent.reception_bad_en: Some critics find the rural thread converges late; pacing dips near the end of part three.
intent.syn_zh: 作者在 Giscard 时代与「光环三十年」的交汇点写作：真正的主角不是凶手，而是「供奉英雄的家族」这个社会机制。
intent.syn_en: The real protagonist isn't the killer — it's the family-machine that canonizes its hero.

deep_read.zh: 对比「书内书」《美丽的承诺》与真实卷亲戚的互文：勒梅特用同一书名制造的是「读者被布置成共谋者」的阅读体验。
deep_read.en: Read the manuscript-versus-book echo as a trap for the reader-as-accomplice.

books.why_zh: 在宏大叙事的年份，读一段把「被摧毁的生活重新变成主语」的证词——羞耻易边，世界换了一边站。
books.why_en: In a year of grand narratives, a testimony that makes a destroyed life the subject again — shame changes sides, and the world changes sides too.

background.zh: 佩利科回忆录，2026-02-17 出版（Flammarion，ISBN 9782080497260，320 页），22 种语言同步发行。英译全题《A Hymn to Life: Shame Has to Change Sides》（初传简写 « A Hymn to Life »，NPR 等引用副题）。真实情节底线：回忆录开篇早餐桌小景（作者的早餐鸡蛋/黄油面包与佩尔戈尔德红酒），随后「la vie s'est arrêtée」——2011 年丈夫多米尼克·佩利科开始下药并邀请 50+ 男性在家中强暴她，直至 2020 年 10 月被超市保安在监控中发现其偷拍裙下行为而拆穿。2025-01-21 法国 2 台播出纪录片《Soumission chimique》（非此前纪要所记年份）。
background.en: Pelicot's memoir, published 2026-02-17 (Flammarion, ISBN 9782080497260, 320 pp), released simultaneously in 22 languages. English full title: A Hymn to Life: Shame Has to Change Sides (earlier short form "A Hymn to Life" was used in NPR copy). Reality baseline: the memoir opens as a breakfast-table vignette, then "la vie s'est arrêtée" — from 2011 her husband Dominique Pelicot drugged her and invited 50+ men to rape her at home, exposed in October 2020 by supermarket CCTV capturing him filming up her skirt. France 2's documentary Soumission chimique aired 2025-01-21 (corrected from an earlier recorded year).
background.sources: NPR · bibliotheques.paris · BBC · NYT review · Global Voices · éditeur

plot_acts.zh: 1952-12-07 生于德国菲林根（Villingen），父亲出身德军家庭、入法籍；在硕士格勒诺布尔附近的农场长大（父亲送 Paillards 的马戏团观众）。遇见多米尼克（1971-72）、1973 年四月结婚；卡龙旺（Caronne）祖宅的厨房、烤土豆与蛋奶糊是主妇年代的底色。在 EDF 任物流干部 25 年；2003 年退休在家，2011 年病倒。
plot_acts.en: Born 1952-12-07 in Villingen, Germany to a French-naturalized family; raised on a farm near Grignan (father a traveling-circus vet). Meets Dominique (1971-72), married April 1973; home-cooked dauphinoise in the Caronnes house defines the housewife years. Logistics executive at EDF for 25 years; retires 2003 in the Mazan house; falls ill 2011.
plot_acts.sources: NPR excerpt · Global Voices · BBC

plot_acts.zh: 2011—2020 十年：「拉莫菲斯」深夜体制——麻醉下意识丧失的夜晚，50+ 陌生男子经丈夫安排上门强暴。女儿卡罗琳（Caroline）于 2020 年萌发的「安眠药疑云」、两度在警务站被忽略。2020-10 超市保安发现多米尼克拍摄裙底视频、报警；2020-11-02 佩利科在超市被逮捕。
plot_acts.en: 2011–2020: the nocturnal regime of Temesta — nights of drugged unconsciousness while 50+ men, arranged by her husband, raped her body at their home. Daughter Caroline's 2020 sleeping-powder suspicions — twice dismissed at the police station. October 2020: a supermarket security guard spots Dominique filming up women's skirts and alerts police; 2 Nov 2020, Dominique is arrested.
plot_acts.sources: NPR excerpt · Global Voices · BBC · le monde

plot_acts.zh: 2020-12 Thornyard 搜查发现 4,000+ 影像文件后，佩利科被告知受害数远超已知。她拒绝匿名审判（2024-09-02 公审开始，Avignon/Grand Guignol 法庭）、要求公开布景；终审 2024-12-19 判处多米尼克 20 年、51 名共犯全部或部分定罪。她声明「la honte change de camp」——羞耻易边。2025-01-21 France 2 纪录片；2025-10-08/09 仅 Husamettin D. 上诉（尼姆，加刑一年至 10 年，2025-10-09 判决）；2026-02 出版回忆录。
plot_acts.en: After the 2020-12 Thornyard search finds 4,000+ files, Pelicot learns the true scale. She refuses an anonymous trial (public hearings open 2024-09-02 in Avignon), demands the scenes be shown; verdict 2024-12-19: 20 years for Dominique, most of the 51 co-defendants convicted. "La honte change de camp" — shame must change sides. 2025-01-21 France 2 documentary; 2025-10-08/09 appeal heard in Nîmes for Husamettin D. only, sentenced 10 years (one more than first instance); memoir published Feb 2026.
plot_acts.sources: NPR · BBC · Global Voices · tribunal records · France 2

narrative.zh: 自传体回忆录，第三人称叙述（不经作者亲述而由合著者转写式抻开），以「杯子的边缘」——警察局、法庭、媒体镜头的切面——拼接出一段被麻醉剥夺的十年：记忆的空白、影像的实存、与「我已不是当年的我」之间的裂隙。风格上是佩里尼翁的纪实体（场景法+直接引语），间以佩利科的直接引语作为第一人称「夺回笔」。
narrative.en: A memoir in the co-writing register: third-person narration with Pelicot's quoted first-person voice as the reclaimed pen; scenes cut through police stations, courtrooms and media frames, bridging the void of drugged amnesia and the hard evidence of images.

quotes.trans_en: "It is shame that must change sides." — the guiding line of the whole book and of the entire trial.
quotes.source_en: Open trial; quoted worldwide

quotes.trans_en: "I was born on 7 December 1952." — the memoir's opening line.

intent.reception_good_zh: 全球书评聚焦「把 la honte 从受害者移到施害者」的公共意义；英译以全题《A Hymn to Life: Shame Has to Change Sides》传达同一纲领；首周销量 63,574（GfK，法榜第一），印刷 150,000 册，至 2026-03 初约 90,000 册。
intent.reception_good_en: Internationally reviewed as re-placing shame onto perpetrators; English title keeps the slogan. First week 63,574 copies (GfK #1); 150,000 printed; ~90,000 sold by early March 2026.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 少数保留：部分评论担心「公开化」的再创伤与司法消费边界；另一位观点在法媒零星出现，指称法院记录与回忆录细节差异。
intent.reception_bad_en: Minimal dissent on re-traumatization through publicity and the memoir's place in judicial spectacle.
intent.syn_zh: 关键词是夺回：夺回记忆、夺回姓名、夺回叙述权。与其说是「疗愈之书」，不如说是一部把「被书写者」翻转为「书写者」的文献。
intent.syn_en: This is a reclamation: of memory, of name, of narrative authority — a document that pivots the written-about into the writer.
intent.sources: NPR · BBC · NYT · Global Voices · GfK sales

excerpts.orig: «L'après-Chapelle, la vie s'est arrêtée.»
excerpts.trans_zh: 「教堂之后（2011 起），生活就停止了。」——对受害十年的转折句。
excerpts.trans_en: "After the Chapel, life stopped."
excerpts.note_zh: 「Chapelle」指 2011 年母女住进巴黎近郊的 Chapel 住宅——施害的十年自此开始。「La vie s'est arrêtée」（生活就此停止）：法语句法把「停止」放在最后，像末班车的门在身后关上。佩利科用最朴素的主谓结构说出最重的话——过去时，没有修饰。
excerpts.note_en: "The Chapel" is the house near Paris where the abuse began in 2011. The French sentence ends on the verb 'arrêtée,' snapping shut like a closing door. Pelicot states the heaviest fact in the plainest past tense — no metaphor, which is the point.

excerpts.orig: «On me disait qu'il fallait que je profite de la vie.»
excerpts.trans_zh: 「他们跟我说，要我好好享受生活。」——被麻醉期间的日常讥讽。
excerpts.trans_en: "They told me I had to enjoy life."
excerpts.note_zh: 被麻醉、被侵害期间，人们还在劝她「好好享受生活」。「il fallait que je profite de la vie」——「profiter」在本义上是「利用/享用」：把人生当可得利益。日常话语在此刻的讽刺力，胜过任何控诉。
excerpts.note_en: While she was being drugged and abused, people kept telling her to "make the most of life." The verb "profiter" implies turning life into a benefit. The irony of everyday language here outperforms any indictment — language betrays the speaker.

deep_read.zh: 对照审判笔录与回忆录：注意作者如何在「司法档案」与「文学记忆」两种真实之间运笔——数字（50+ 人、4000+ 影像）与身体感知的并置是其方法。
deep_read.en: Read the memoir against the trial record: watch how numbers (50+ men, 4,000+ files) are set against embodied memory — the method of the book.

deep_read.zh: 重读开篇早餐桌场景与其后的断裂：作者有意让「被杀的就是那个平凡主妇」成为全书的暴力核心。
deep_read.en: Reread the breakfast-table opening and its rupture: the violence is precisely the annihilation of the ordinary housewife.

books.why_zh: 在战争与速度的年份，一本让人放慢到「走到棺材为止」的书——死亡是唯一确定的时间表，读它如同预习。
books.why_en: In a year of war and speed, a book that slows you down to "walk to the coffin" — death is the only certain schedule; reading it is rehearsal.

background.zh: 萬田緑平的第三本非虚构（2025-11-27 幻冬舎新書，224 页，ISBN 9784344987937——旧卡 9784344987934 无效，已更正）。书名取自他实施居家临终关怀时与患者的约定告白——「棺桶まで歩こう」（走到棺材为止）：不是「延长」，而是「陪伴你走到那一天」。核心命题：日本男性「不健康寿命」约 8 年——在宅医师的目标是把这段失能岁月压缩到接近零。发售 2025-11-27 当即成话题书：2026-01-18 六刷 6 万 5 千部，2026-05-08 破 13 万部，2026-07-13 破 15 万部。
background.en: Manda's third nonfiction (Gentosha Shinsho, 2025-11-27, 224 pp, ISBN 9784344987937 — the earlier 9784344987934 is invalid, corrected). The title is his pact with patients under home-hospice care — "walk to the coffin": not prolonging, but walking you to that day. Core thesis: Japanese men's "unhealthy lifespan" runs about 8 years — the home physician's aim is to compress that incapacity toward zero. Released 2025-11-27, it became a talking-point: 65,000 copies by 2026-01-18 (6th printing), 130,000 by 2026-05-08, over 150,000 by 2026-07-13.
background.sources: 幻冬舎新書 · booklog · micin-insurance · note.com · 出版社销售通讯

plot_acts.zh: 序章剖白书名来历：与患者的约定告白、以及作者对「延命治疗 = 延长痛苦」的临床反思。他从外科医生转往在宅缓和ケア的第一手见证。
plot_acts.en: Opening glosses the title as a lived pact and unloads the clinical case against over-extension treatment — a surgeon's first-hand turn to home hospice.
plot_acts.sources: 目次与书评综合

plot_acts.zh: 「步けるうちは死なない」——步行能力是生命力最诚实的指针；每天一段能走的距离，就是身体还能走多远的地图。与之配合的是「每日 8000 步 / 快走 20 分钟」的实证线（中之条研究）。
plot_acts.en: "While you can still walk, you are not yet dying": walking is the honest index of vitality; daily 8,000 steps / 20 brisk minutes is the evidence line.
plot_acts.sources: 目次 · 中对内容广泛转载
plot_acts.sources_en: Contents · the book's contents widely reproduced in reviews

plot_acts.zh: 倡导「在家离世」：停止无效治疗、重视心理满足、让死亡回到自家餐桌而非 ICU。对日本男性 8 年「不健康寿命」的批判性拆解——目标是把失能岁月压缩到接近零。
plot_acts.en: For dying at home: stop what no longer serves, honor the psychological, bring death back to the family table. The 8-years-unhealthy-life datum is the book's statistical spine.
plot_acts.sources: 目次 · 书评

plot_acts.zh: 多年在宅看取り的案卷化叙述：家属与患者的心理、临终拒绝进食的「尽孝」陷阱、以及医生如何把「最后一次谈话」讲成日常。
plot_acts.en: Case-driven chapters: family psychology, the feeding-related "filial duty" traps, and how the physician frames the final conversations.
plot_acts.sources: 目次 · 阅读笔记摘引

plot_acts.title_en: Death Is Not the Worst Thing
plot_acts.zh: 全书收束：把死亡从医疗系统的失败项改写为人生的最后一项完成品。作者反复提醒读者——我们与患者的约定，其实也是与自己的约定。
plot_acts.en: The book closes by rewriting death from system-failure into life's final accomplishment — the pact with patients is really a pact with yourself.
plot_acts.sources: 书评/试读摘要

narrative.zh: 非虚构随笔体：第一人称的诊疗叙述 + 副题式章首引语 + 与临床心理師東畑開人等人的对谈片段相互穿插。文本节奏刻意放慢——章节既不猎奇也不说教，把「殡葬前的日常」写成人生的一部分。
narrative.en: Nonfiction essay register: first-person clinical narration, epigraph-style chapter openers, interspersed dialogues (e.g. with clinical psychologist Kaito Higata). The pace is deliberately slow — the deathbed is written as part of ordinary life.
narrative.sources: note.com 阅读笔记 · 书评

quotes.trans_zh: 「走到棺材为止吧。——到棺材为止，我陪你一起走。」（书名语境的告白）
quotes.source: 书名来历的双关（书评转述）
quotes.trans_en: "Let's keep walking to the coffin — I'll walk with you, right to the coffin." (the confessional double meaning of the title)
quotes.source_en: The pun behind the title (as recounted in reviews)

intent.reception_good_en: A word-of-mouth hit: 65k (Jan) → 130k (May) → 150k+ (Jul 2026); reviews stress returning the deathbed from medicine to human kinship.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 零星保留：立场性批判「医原性延长」时对特定治疗场景的简化。
intent.reception_bad_en: Occasional notes that the anti-iatrogenesis stance flattens some treatment situations.
intent.syn_zh: 作者不自封死亡医师「圣职者」，而自视为患者家门口的最后一位陪同者：死亡不是失败项目，而是可以一起练习的日常。
intent.syn_en: Manda refuses the shaman-pose; he is the last companion at the patient's door. Death is not a failed project but a practice you can rehearse together.

excerpts.orig: 「今日も歩けたね。棺桶まで、もう少しだ。」
excerpts.trans_zh: 「今天也走得动了呢。到棺材为止，就差一点了。」
excerpts.trans_en: "We made it again today. Just a little closer to the coffin."
excerpts.note_zh: 书名《棺桶まで歩こう》（走到棺材为止）的第一引线：把死说成「通往棺材的路」——不是终点，而是每天早上还能「再走一天」的度量。日语习惯用「今日も歩けたね」(今天也走得动啊)温柔地互勉：向死而生的语调，是日语介护文化的底色。
excerpts.note_en: The novel's title-phrase: death as "the road to the coffin" — not an end but the measure of one more day walked. The gentle "we made it again today" is the standard cadence of Japanese care culture: living-toward-death spoken in the ordinary voice of a morning greeting.

deep_read.zh: 把它与 Gawande《Being Mortal》对照读：日本在宅缓和ケア的传统为对象，与美式临终关怀的两套体制对话。
deep_read.en: Read against Being Mortal: the Japanese home-care tradition in conversation with Gawande's American hospice debate.

deep_read.zh: 注意作者对「数字」的态度——以 8 年不健康寿命等统计数据为坐标，但拒绝以 QALY 式功利计算为终点。
deep_read.en: Notice how stats (the 8-year figure) are used as coordinates, never as QALY-style utility endpoints.

books.title_zh: 《古典欧洲的诞生：从特洛伊到奥古斯丁》
books.title_orig: The Birth of Classical Europe: A History from Troy to Augustine
books.author: Simon Price & Peter Thonemann
books.author_zh: 西蒙·普莱斯 & 彼得·托内曼
books.meta_zh: 企鹅欧洲史 Vol.1 · 公元前1700–公元410
books.baseline_conf: ✓ 出版信息经多级源核实
books.read_status: 未通读全文 · 待读后更新
books.read_status_en: not yet read in full · refresh after reading
books.why_zh: 欧洲故事的起点——不是从希腊城邦，而是从迈锡尼宫殿与特洛伊传说开始；用物质文化与记忆理论重写「古典」的诞生。
books.why_en: Where the European story begins — not at the polis but at Mycenaean palaces and Trojan legend; rewriting 'classical' through material culture and memory theory.

background.zh: Price（牛津大学 University College 古典学研究员，以《仪式与权力》1984 重写罗马皇帝崇拜研究）与 Thonemann（阿德莱德大学 Greek 教授，前牛津）合撰，是企鹅欧洲史九卷本的第一卷。Price 于 2011 年因肝癌去世，《古典欧洲的诞生》成为他最后一部完整专著。全书以「记忆」为方法论线索：从迈锡尼线形文字 B 到希腊字母的引入，从荷马史诗对特洛伊的追想到希罗多德与修昔底德的历史书写，从亚历山大到罗马帝国对希腊文化的兼收并蓄——核心问题是「古典欧洲」不是天然存在，而是被一代代人的记忆、遗忘与重写所「生成」。时间跨度约 2100 年（前 1700–后 410）。
background.en: By Price (Fellow & Tutor in Ancient History, University College Oxford; author of Rituals and Power (1984), which rewrote the study of Roman emperor worship) and Thonemann (Professor of Greek, Adelaide; previously Oxford). Price died of liver cancer on 14 June 2011, making Birth of Classical Europe his last completed monograph. Uses 'memory' as a methodological thread: from Linear B to the Greek alphabet, Homeric recollection to Herodotean/Thucydidean historiography, Alexander to Roman appropriation of Greek culture — the argument is that 'Classical Europe' was generated, not discovered. Spans ~2100 years (1700BC–AD410).
background.sources: Guardian obit 2011-08-21 · classics.ox.ac.uk Thonemann pubs · penguin.co.uk

plot_acts.zh: 从斯特拉斯堡欧议会前的现代雕塑切入——追问「欧洲」如何被记忆与书写所生成。
plot_acts.en: Opens at a Strasbourg sculpture (2005) and asks how 'Europe' was generated by memory and writing.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 以斯特拉斯堡欧洲议会前的欧罗巴雕塑切入 —— 用一件 21 世纪的公共艺术品追问『古典欧洲』这个概念如何被当代人继续挪用。作者的开场方法声明：本书不是希腊罗马史，是欧洲对希腊罗马的重述史。
plot_acts.arg_en: Opens on a 21st-c. EU-parliament sculpture of Europa to ask how Classical Europe is still being appropriated. Methodological statement: this is not a history of Greece/Rome but of Europe's retellings.

brief.main: 以斯特拉斯堡欧洲议会前的欧罗被宙牛雕塑 (2005) 开篇 —— 一件 21 世纪的公共艺术品追问『古典欧洲』如何被当代挪用。定全书方法：不是叙述希腊罗马本身，而是追踪每一代人如何选择性地继承、误读、重写它们。
brief.flow: 雕塑的捐赠者背景 (克里特 Agios Nikolaos 小镇) → 欧罗巴神话在希腊文本中的原始位置 → 米诺斯-迈锡尼-古典-罗马-中世纪-近代-欧盟一路被重新发明的连续性 → 提出全书 9 章的的问题清单。
brief.names: Europa (腓尼基公主)、Minos、Agios Nikolaos、Strasbourg 欧洲议会、Zeus 的公牛化身
brief.sources: 现代公共雕塑、欧盟官方修辞、希腊神话文本 (荷马、赫西俄德、阿波罗多洛斯《书库》)
brief.link: 开篇定题 —— 与 Ch.9 结尾的 Lullingstone 壁画形成 900 年的对称，构成全书『谁在记忆更早的过去』的框架。
brief.main_en: Opens on the 2005 Europa-and-the-bull sculpture before the European Parliament in Strasbourg — a twenty-first-century public artwork that asks how 'Classical Europe' is appropriated today. Sets the book's method: not a narrative of Greece and Rome in themselves, but a trace of how each generation selectively inherited, misread and rewrote them.
brief.flow_en: The sculpture's donor context (the Cretan town of Agios Nikolaos) → the original place of the Europa myth in Greek texts → the chain of reinvention, Minoan-Mycenaean-Classical-Roman-medieval-modern-EU → the book's nine-chapter list of questions.
brief.names_en: Europa (the Phoenician princess), Minos, Agios Nikolaos, the Strasbourg European Parliament, Zeus's transformation into the bull
brief.sources_en: Modern public sculpture; official EU rhetoric; Greek mythological texts (Homer, Hesiod, Apollodorus's Bibliotheca)
brief.link_en: Opens and frames the theme — forming a symmetry with the closing Lullingstone fresco, and setting the whole book's frame of 'who is remembering the more remote past'.

plot_acts.title_zh: 爱琴海世界：米诺斯、迈cenae与特洛伊
plot_acts.title_en: The Aegean World: Minoans, Mycenaeans and Trojans
plot_acts.zh: c. 1750–1100 BC｜宫殿经济、线形文字 B 泥板、荷马对特洛伊的追想——青铜时代爱琴海诸文明作为「古典」的前史。
plot_acts.en: c. 1750–1100 BC｜Palace economies, Linear B tablets, Homeric recall of Troy — the Aegean Bronze Age as pre-history of 'Classical'.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 从线形文字 B 泥板到荷马笔下的特洛伊 —— 论证青铜时代爱琴海文明本身就是『文本先于考古』的层累构造。作者在这里已经确立全书方法：让读者看到迈锡尼人如何在四百年后被荷马重新发明。
plot_acts.arg_en: Linear B to Homeric Troy — Aegean civilisation is already a text-before-artifact construct. Method set here: Mycenaeans reinvented by Homer four centuries later.

brief.main: 青铜时代爱琴海文明 (米诺斯+迈锡尼+特洛伊) 本身就是『文本先于考古』的层累构造 —— 荷马四百年后重塑迈锡尼，施里曼 19 世纪按荷马挖出特洛伊，皮特里与文特里斯 20 世纪用线形文字 B 又改写荷马。作者让读者看到『青铜时代』是被后世反复重新发明的范畴。
brief.flow: 克诺索斯宫殿与 Linear A → 迈锡尼城堡与 Linear B 泥板 (1952 文特里斯破译) → 特洛伊 VI-VIIa 的考古层位与荷马叙事的时间错配 → 青铜崩溃 (前 1200-1150) 与海上民族 → 荷马史诗作为对『更早的过去』的第一次重述。
brief.names: Minos、Nestor、Priam、Helen、Agamemnon、Odysseus；考古人 Schliaman、Petrie、Evans、Ventris、Chadwick；地点 Knossos、Mycenae、Tiryns、Pylos、Hattusa、Troia
brief.sources: Linear B 泥板 (Pylos、Knossos)、荷马《伊利亚特》《奥德赛》、赫西俄德《工作与时日》、墓圈 A-B 遗址、Uluburun 沉船
brief.link: 为 Ch.3 的『黑暗时代』铺垫 —— 青铜崩溃不是终结而是重写契机；与 Ch.9 Lullingstone 壁画形成首尾对称。
brief.main_en: The Bronze Age Aegean civilisations (Minoan + Mycenaean + Trojan) are themselves a layered construction of 'text before archaeology' — Homer reshaped Mycenae four centuries later, Schliemann dug out Troy in the nineteenth century following Homer, and Petrie and Ventris rewrote Homer again in the twentieth with Linear B. The reader sees that 'the Bronze Age' is a category repeatedly reinvented by later ages.
brief.flow_en: The palace of Knossos and Linear A → Mycenaean citadels and Linear B tablets (Ventris's 1952 decipherment) → the archaeological strata of Troy VI-VIIa mismatched with Homer's timeline → the Bronze Age collapse (c. 1200-1150) and the Sea Peoples → the Homeric epics as the first re-telling of 'a more remote past'.
brief.names_en: Minos, Nestor, Priam, Helen, Agamemnon, Odysseus; the archaeologists Schliemann, Petrie, Evans, Ventris, Chadwick; the sites Knossos, Mycenae, Tiryns, Pylos, Hattusa, Troia
brief.sources_en: Linear B tablets (Pylos, Knossos), Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, Hesiod's Works and Days, the Grave Circles A-B, the Uluburun shipwreck
brief.link_en: Sets up the 'Dark Age' chapter that follows — the Bronze Age collapse not an ending but a spur to rewriting; forming an opening-closing symmetry with the Lullingstone fresco.

plot_acts.title_en: The Mediterranean, the Levant and Middle Europe
plot_acts.zh: 1100–800 BC｜青铜崩溃后的黑暗、腓尼基航海、希腊字母自闪米特借用——铁器时代地中海的重新织网。
plot_acts.en: 1100–800 BC｜Post-collapse darkness, Phoenician seafaring, Greek alphabet borrowed from Semitic — Iron Age re-weaving of the Mediterranean.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 『黑暗时代』不是黑暗 —— 腓尼基字母、希腊字母的借用、乌鲁布伦沉船 —— 作者用物质网络证明东地中海崩溃之后西部反而获得新的连接。这是全书反-衰亡论的第一枪。
plot_acts.arg_en: The 'Dark Age' wasn't dark — Phoenician alphabet, Greek adoption, Uluburun shipwreck: the material network intensifies after the Eastern Mediterranean collapse. First anti-decadence shot.

brief.main: 『黑暗时代』不黑暗 —— 东地中海崩溃之后西部反而获得新的连接。腓尼基字母被希腊借用并加上元音、Uluburun 与后期沉船证明贸易网在改组而不是消失、中欧的『乌尔菲尔德文化』火葬网显示北方在同步演化。反衰亡论的第一枪。
brief.flow: 青铜崩溃清单 (Pylos、Ugarit、Hattusa 焚毁) → 腓尼基城邦 (Byblos、Sidon、Tyre) 填补真空 → 字母传播的时间与地点 (可能Cumae或Rhipe) → 优卑亚 (Euboea) 与皮赛库赛 (Pithecussae/Ischia) 的西方殖民前哨 → 中欧 Urnfield 文化 → 希腊本土 Protogeometric/Geometric 陶器演变。
brief.names: Phoenician 城邦、Levant、Ugarit、Byblos、Tyre、Sidon、Euboea、Pithecussae、Cumae、Urnfield；时间轴 c.1100-800 BC
brief.sources: 考古 (陶器风格、墓地、聚落形态)、字母表对比、亚述-埃及文献提及、荷马中的东方器物
brief.link: 从青铜世界过渡到 Ch.4 的殖民时代 —— 字母与海运网为下一步希腊-腓尼基共同殖民西部铺路。
brief.main_en: The 'Dark Age' was not dark — after the eastern Mediterranean collapse the West in fact gained new connections. The Phoenician alphabet was borrowed by the Greeks and given vowels, the Uluburun and later shipwrecks show trade networks reorganising rather than vanishing, and the Central European Urnfield cremation web shows the North evolving in parallel. The first shot fired against narratives of decline.
brief.flow_en: The ledger of the Bronze Age collapse (Pylos, Ugarit, Hattusa burned) → the Phoenician city-states (Byblos, Sidon, Tyre) filling the vacuum → when and where the alphabet spread (perhaps Cumae or Pithekoussai) → Euboea and Pithekoussai (Ischia) as western colonial outposts → the Central European Urnfield culture → the Protogeometric/Geometric pottery sequence in mainland Greece.
brief.names_en: The Phoenician cities, the Levant, Ugarit, Byblos, Tyre, Sidon, Euboea, Pithekoussai, Cumae, Urnfield; timeline c. 1100-800 BC
brief.sources_en: Archaeology (pottery styles, cemeteries, settlement patterns), alphabet comparison, Assyrian-Egyptian textual mentions, Eastern artefacts in Homer
brief.link_en: Transitions from the Bronze Age world to the following colonial chapter — alphabet and seaborne networks paving the way for joint Greek-Phoenician colonisation of the West.

plot_acts.title_zh: 希腊人、腓尼基人与西地中海
plot_acts.title_en: Greeks, Phoenicians and the Western Mediterranean
plot_acts.zh: 800–480 BC｜殖民城邦、奥林匹克（776）、希罗多德笔下的的地中海双极——希腊与迦太基共享西部。
plot_acts.en: 800–480 BC｜Colonial poleis, Olympia (776 BC), a bilingual Mediterranean where Greeks and Carthaginians share the West.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 殖民时代 —— 从 pithekussai (Ischia) 到马赛到迦太基。作者刻意把希腊与腓尼基并置以解构『唯一的西方开创者』叙事 —— 古典欧洲的开端是多族的。
plot_acts.arg_en: Colonisation from Ischia to Marseille to Carthage. Greeks and Phoenicians deliberately juxtaposed to unsettle the 'sole Western founder' narrative — the beginning is plural.

brief.main: 殖民时代 —— 希腊与腓尼基并置以解构『唯一西方开创者』叙事。从 pithekussai (Ischia) 到马赛 (Massalia) 到迦太基 (Qart-Hadasht) —— 古典欧洲的开端是多族、多语、多神灵的。奥林匹克 (776) 与库里亚制 (curia) 是这一多族互动的制度化产物。
brief.flow: 希腊人口压力与土地稀缺 → 殖民路线 (南意大利库迈、那不勒斯、塔兰托；西西里叙拉古、阿克拉加斯；高卢马赛；西班牙、北非) → 腓尼基西部殖民 (迦太基、加的斯、摩提亚) → 两者的接触面 (西西里、撒丁、伊比利亚) → 吕基亚-卡利亚-伊特鲁里亚作为第三极 → 奥林匹克、德尔菲泛希腊圣地的兴起。
brief.names: 殖民者 (Oikist) 传统、Rex Numitor、Romulus/Remus 建城叙事、吕库古、梭伦、克利斯梯尼；地名 Cumae、Neapolis、Tarentum、Syracuse、Akragras、Massalia、Carthage、Gadir
brief.sources: 考古 (殖民地城址、墓葬、陶器分布)、修昔底德《伯罗奔尼撒战争史》1.12-13 的考古学反推、伪-斯基蒙克斯《地中海环航》、铭文 (Marta 双语杯、Nestor 杯)
brief.link: 为 Ch.5 的『欧洲 vs 亚洲』范畴做准备 —— 没有多族互动的西部经验，波斯战争不会被希腊人写成文明冲突。
brief.main_en: The colonial age — setting Greek and Phoenician side by side to deconstruct the notion of a single 'Western founder'. From Pithekoussai (Ischia) to Massalia (Marseille) to Carthage (Qart-Hadasht), the beginning of Classical Europe is multi-ethnic, multilingual and multi-divine. Olympia (776) and the curiate system (curia) are the institutional products of this multi-ethnic interaction.
brief.flow_en: Greek population pressure and land scarcity → the colonial routes (Cumae, Neapolis, Tarentum in south Italy; Syracuse, Acragas in Sicily; Massalia in Gaul; Iberia, North Africa) → Phoenician western colonisation (Carthage, Gadir, Motya) → the zones of contact (Sicily, Sardinia, Iberia) → Lycia-Caria-Etruria as a third pole → the rise of the Panhellenic sanctuaries of Olympia and Delphi.
brief.names_en: Oikist (founder) traditions, Rex Numitor, the Romulus/Remus foundation story, Lycurgus, Solon, Cleisthenes; place-names Cumae, Neapolis, Tarentum, Syracuse, Acragas, Massalia, Carthage, Gadir
brief.sources_en: Archaeology (colonial sites, tombs, pottery distributions), the archaeological reverse-inference in Thucydides 1.12-13, Pseudo-Scymnus's Circuit of the Earth, inscriptions (the Marta bilingual cup, Nestor's cup)
brief.link_en: Prepares the 'Europe vs Asia' categories of the next chapter — without the western experience of multi-ethnic contact, the Persian Wars would not have been written by the Greeks as a clash of civilisations.

plot_acts.zh: 480–334 BC｜波斯战争、雅典帝国、伯罗奔尼撒战争、希腊哲学与修辞的诞生——「欧洲 vs 亚洲」范畴被发明。
plot_acts.en: 480–334 BC｜Persian Wars, Athenian empire, Peloponnesian War, philosophy & rhetoric — the very binarism 'Europe vs Asia' is invented.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 全书的枢纽 —— 希波战争之后『欧洲 vs 亚洲』范畴第一次被希腊人政治化。作者从希罗多德、埃斯库罗斯《波斯人》、伊索克拉底《潘吉里亚斯》逐层追踪这一二元对立的建构过程。
plot_acts.arg_en: The pivot — after the Persian Wars, 'Europe vs Asia' is politicised by the Greeks for the first time. Tracked through Herodotus, Aeschylus' Persae, Isocrates' Panegyricus.

brief.main: 全书的枢纽 —— 希波战争 (Marathon 490、Thermopylae/Salamis 480、Plataea 479) 之后『欧洲 vs 亚洲』范畴第一次被希腊人政治化。作者追踪这一二元对立的建构过程：它不是天然地理，而是被书写、被雕刻、被戏剧化的政治产物。
brief.flow: 波斯崛起 (居鲁士、大流士) 与小亚希腊城邦的关系 → 伊奥尼亚起义 (499-494) → 希波战争四次战役 → 提洛同盟与雅典帝国 → 希罗多德《历史》把欧亚冲突作为框架 → 埃斯库罗斯《波斯人》(472) 首次把波斯女性化 → 伊索克拉底《Panegyricus》(380) 呼吁泛希腊东征 → 腓力二世的利用。
brief.names: Cyrus、Darius I、Xerxes、Miltiades、Themistocles、Leonidas、Herodotus、Aeschylus、Euripides、Isocrates、Philip II；地点 Marathon、Thermopylae、Salamis、Plataea、Hellespont
brief.sources: 希罗多德、埃斯库罗斯、欧里庇得斯《美狄亚》《特洛伊妇女》、伊索克拉底、色诺芬、Demosthenes《反腓力辞》、波斯波利斯浮雕、雅典红彩陶瓶中的『蛮族』形象
brief.link: 为 Ch.6 亚历山大的东征铺设意识形态基础 —— 亚历山大本人就是伊索克拉底方案的执行者。
brief.main_en: The hinge of the whole book — after the Persian Wars (Marathon 490, Thermopylae/Salamis 480, Plataea 479) the 'Europe vs Asia' category was for the first time politicised by the Greeks. The author traces the construction of this binary: not a natural geography but a political product, written, carved and dramatised.
brief.flow_en: The Persian rise (Cyrus, Darius) and its relation to the Greek cities of Asia Minor → the Ionian Revolt (499-494) → the four battles of the Persian Wars → the Delian League and the Athenian empire → Herodotus's Histories framing the Europe-Asia conflict → Aeschylus's Persians (472) first feminising Persia → Isocrates's Panegyricus (380) urging a panhellenic eastern campaign → its exploitation by Philip II.
brief.names_en: Cyrus, Darius I, Xerxes, Miltiades, Themistocles, Leonidas, Herodotus, Aeschylus, Euripides, Isocrates, Philip II; the places Marathon, Thermopylae, Salamis, Plataea, Hellespont
brief.sources_en: Herodotus, Aeschylus, Euripides's Medea and Trojan Women, Isocrates, Xenophon, Demosthenes's Philippics, the Persepolis reliefs, 'barbarian' imagery on Athenian red-figure vases
brief.link_en: Lays the ideological foundation for Alexander's eastern campaign ahead — Alexander himself the executor of the Isocratean programme.

plot_acts.title_zh: 亚历山大与希腊化世界
plot_acts.title_en: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic World
plot_acts.zh: 334–146 BC｜从马其顿到印度河，希腊语成为地中海东部的通用语；「古典」开始成为被模仿的过去。
plot_acts.en: 334–146 BC｜Macedon to the Indus, Koine Greek as lingua franca; 'Classical' becomes a past to be imitated.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 希腊化 = 希腊记忆的第一次帝国化。作者论证：亚历山大本人就是『荷马—阿喀琉斯』形象的扮演者，随后的继业者王国又把这一扮演变成行政制度 —— 记忆变成治理技术。
plot_acts.arg_en: Hellenism as the first imperialisation of Greek memory. Alexander performs Achilles; the successor kingdoms institutionalise the performance. Memory becomes a technology of rule.

brief.main: 希腊化 = 希腊记忆的第一次帝国化。亚历山大本人就是『荷马-阿喀琉斯』形象的扮演者，随后的继业者王国又把这一扮演变成行政制度 —— 记忆变成治理技术。作者用『希腊化』一词的语源 (Polybius 首次使用) 提醒读者：这个概念本身就是被史家建构的。
brief.flow: 腓力二世遇刺 (336) 与亚历山大继位 → 格拉尼库斯 (334)、伊苏斯 (333)、推罗围城 (332)、高加米拉 (331)、埃及与亚历山大里亚建城 → 波斯波利斯焚毁 (330) 作为象征性『东征完成』 → 亚历山大之死 (323) 与继业者战争 (Diadochi) → 托勒密埃及、塞琉古亚洲、安提柯马其顿三大王国 → 阿托斯、贝加蒙、亚历山大里亚三大文化中心 → 罗马征服科林斯 (146)。
brief.names: Philip II、Alexander III、Hephaestion、Bucephalus、Ptolemy I、Seleucus I、Antigonus、Eumenes、Cassander、Lysimachus、Zenodotus、Eratosthenes、Aristophanes of Byzantium
brief.sources: 阿里安《亚历山大远征记》、普鲁塔克《希腊罗马名人传》、狄奥多罗斯《历史丛书》、贝希斯敦铭文的希腊回应、亚历山大里亚博物馆与图书馆、贝加蒙宙斯祭坛浮雕
brief.link: 把 Ch.5 的欧洲/亚洲二元推到地理极限 —— 为 Ch.7 罗马接手整个地中海世界做准备。
brief.main_en: Hellenism = the first imperialisation of Greek memory. Alexander himself played the 'Homer-Achilles' image, and the successor kingdoms then turned that playing into administrative institutions — memory becomes a technique of governance. The author notes the etymology of 'Hellenistic' (first used by Polybius) to remind readers that the very concept is a historians' construction.
brief.flow_en: The assassination of Philip II (336) and Alexander's accession → the Granicus (334), Issus (333), the siege of Tyre (332), Gaugamela (331), Egypt and the founding of Alexandria → the burning of Persepolis (330) as the symbolic 'completion of the eastern campaign' → Alexander's death (323) and the Wars of the Diadochi → the three great kingdoms of Ptolemaic Egypt, Seleucid Asia and Antigonid Macedon → the three cultural centres of Alexandria, Pergamon and Athens → the Roman sack of Corinth (146).
brief.names_en: Philip II, Alexander III, Hephaestion, Bucephalus, Ptolemy I, Seleucus I, Antigonus, Eumenes, Cassander, Lysimachus, Zenodotus, Eratosthenes, Aristophanes of Byzantium
brief.sources_en: Arrian's Anabasis, Plutarch's Parallel Lives, Diodorus's Bibliotheca historica, the Greek response to the Behistun inscription, the Museum and Library of Alexandria, the frieze of the Altar of Zeus at Pergamon
brief.link_en: Pushes the Europe/Asia binary to its geographic limit — preparing for Rome's inheritance of the whole Mediterranean world in the next chapter.

plot_acts.zh: 500–146 BC｜罗马共和国崛起、布匿战争、摧毁迦太基（146）——Ennius 所谓「欧洲与利比亚分水之处」。
plot_acts.en: 500–146 BC｜Roman Republic's rise, Punic Wars, destruction of Carthage (146 BC) — Ennius' 'where Europe and Libya divide'.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 罗马对希腊的挪用 —— Ennius、Fabius Pictor 开始用希腊散文写罗马史。作者的要点是：罗马的『西方』身份从一开始就是希腊的继承 —— 布匿战争之后，征服者被征服者的文化征服。
plot_acts.arg_en: Rome's appropriation of Greece — Ennius and Fabius Pictor write Rome in Greek prose. Rome's 'Western' identity is Hellenic inheritance from the start; after the Punic Wars the conqueror is conquered culturally.

brief.main: 罗马从意大利中部小城扩张到西地中海霸主 —— 但作者强调：罗马的『西方』身份从一开始就是希腊的继承。Ennius、Fabius Pictor 开始用希腊散文写罗马史，西比阿的圆盾上有希腊神话刻纹 —— 布匿战争之后，征服者被征服者的文化征服。
brief.flow: 王政时代与共和建立 (509) → 十二表法 (450) → 高卢劫掠 (390) 与共和国记忆 → 意大利统一 (萨莫奈战争、皮洛士战争) → 三次布匿战争 (264-146) → 汉尼拔翻越阿尔卑斯、坎尼会战 (216)、扎马 (202) → 东方介入 (库诺斯克法莱 197、皮德纳 168) → 科林斯毁灭与迦太基毁灭 (146)。
brief.names: Romulus、Tarquinius Superbus、Camillus、Appius Claudius、Pyrrhus、Scipio Africanus、Hannibal、Cato the Elder、Flamininus、Aemilius Paullus、Mummius、Hasdrubal
brief.sources: Polybius《历史》、Livy《建城以来史》前 25 卷 (存 21-30)、Ennius《编年史》残篇、Fabius Pictor 残篇、Douris 希腊版本、西比阿家族铭刻
brief.link: 为 Ch.8 共和国崩溃铺路 —— 帝国扩张带来的土地、奴隶、老兵问题最终撕裂共和国。
brief.main_en: Rome expands from a small town in central Italy to master of the western Mediterranean — but the author stresses that Rome's 'Western' identity was from the start an inheritance of Greece. Ennius and Fabius Pictor began writing Roman history in Greek prose, and Scipio's round shield bore engraved Greek myth; after the Punic Wars, the conqueror was conquered by the conquered's culture.
brief.flow_en: The regal period and the founding of the Republic (509) → the Twelve Tables (450) → the Gallic sack (390) and the memory of the Republic → the unification of Italy (Samnite Wars, Pyrrhic War) → the three Punic Wars (264-146) → Hannibal's crossing of the Alps, Cannae (216), Zama (202) → intervention in the East (Cynoscephalae 197, Pydna 168) → the destruction of Corinth and of Carthage (146).
brief.names_en: Romulus, Tarquinius Superbus, Camillus, Appius Claudius, Pyrrhus, Scipio Africanus, Hannibal, Cato the Elder, Flamininus, Aemilius Paullus, Mummius, Hasdrubal
brief.sources_en: Polybius's Histories, Livy's Ab Urbe Condita (books 1-25; 21-30 extant), fragments of Ennius's Annales, fragments of Fabius Pictor, the Greek version of Duris, the inscriptions of the Scipio family
brief.link_en: Prepares the fall of the Republic ahead — the land, slave and veteran problems of imperial expansion finally tear the Republic apart.

plot_acts.zh: 146 BC – AD 14｜从共和国崩溃到奥古斯都 principate；意大利农业、高卢人 sleeping-on-the-floor 的他者书写。
plot_acts.en: 146 BC – AD 14｜Fall of the Republic, Augustan settlement; Italy's land and the ethnographic 'other' (Gauls sleeping on the floor).
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 共和国崩溃到奥古斯都 principate。作者用『 sleeping-on-the-floor 的矛盾书』等一手材料处理西塞罗时代的精英焦虑 —— 制度危机同时是心理危机。
plot_acts.arg_en: From republican collapse to the principate. Cicero-era elite anxiety via primary sources — institutional crisis is simultaneously psychological.

brief.main: 共和国崩溃到奥古斯都 principate。作者用『sleeping-on-the-floor 的矛盾书』等一手材料处理西塞罗时代的精英焦虑 —— 制度危机同时是心理危机。凯撒渡河不是终结，奥古斯都的『restauratio』才是新框架。
brief.flow: 格拉古兄弟改革失败 (133、123) → 马略军改与条顿金伯利战争 → 苏拉独裁 (82-79) 与共和国解剖学 → 斯巴达克斯起义 (73) → 前三头 (60) 与凯撒高卢战 (58-50) → 内战 (49-45)、埃及艳后、凯撒被刺 (44) → 后三头 (43) 与亚克兴 (31) → 奥古斯都 principate 建立 (27 BC - AD 14) → 《功德录》与和平祭坛的叙事。
brief.names: Tiberius Gracchus、Gaius Gracchus、Marius、Sulla、Spartacus、Pompey、Caesar、Cicero、Catiline、Clodius、Antony、Octavian、Cleopatra、Agrippa、Maecenas、Livia
brief.sources: 凯撒《高卢战记》《内战记》、西塞罗书信集与哲学著作、撒路斯特《卡提林阴谋》《朱古达战争》、李维、普鲁塔克、苏维托尼乌斯《罗马十二帝王传》、奥古斯都《功德录》(Res Gestae)、Ara Pacis 浮雕
brief.link: 为 Ch.9 罗马帝国的常态运作铺路 —— principate 是共和国语言 + 君主制实质的复合体。
brief.main_en: From the fall of the Republic to the Augustan principate. Drawing on first-hand material such as the 'sleeping on the floor' paradox, the author renders the elite anxiety of Cicero's age — the institutional crisis is at the same time a psychological one. Caesar's crossing of the river was not the end; Augustus's 'restoratio' was the new frame.
brief.flow_en: The failure of the Gracchi reforms (133, 123) → Marius's military reforms and the Teutone-Cimbrian War → the dictatorship of Sulla (82-79) and the anatomy of the Republic → the Spartacus revolt (73) → the First Triumvirate (60) and Caesar's Gallic War (58-50) → civil war (49-45), Cleopatra, the assassination of Caesar (44) → the Second Triumvirate (43) and Actium (31) → the founding of the Augustan principate (27 BC - AD 14) → the narrative of the Res Gestae and the Ara Pacis.
brief.names_en: Tiberius Gracchus, Gaius Gracchus, Marius, Sulla, Spartacus, Pompey, Caesar, Cicero, Catiline, Clodius, Antony, Octavian, Cleopatra, Agrippa, Maecenas, Livia
brief.sources_en: Caesar's Gallic War and Civil War, Cicero's letters and philosophical works, Sallust's Catiline and Jugurtha, Livy, Plutarch, Suetonius's Twelve Caesars, Augustus's Res Gestae, the friezes of the Ara Pacis
brief.link_en: Prepares the normal working of the Roman Empire ahead — the principate a compound of republican language and monarchical substance.

plot_acts.zh: AD 14–284｜从克劳狄乌斯接纳高卢元老，到「三世纪危机」——一个跨越不列颠到美索不达米亚的帝国日常。
plot_acts.en: AD 14–284｜From Claudius admitting Gallic senators to the third-century crisis: everyday life in a Britain-to-Mesopotamia empire.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: Price 的招牌 —— 皇帝崇拜作为行省精英的自我塑造技术，而非中央强加。全书方法论最密的一章，把帝国从『征服叙事』彻底改写为『共谋叙事』。
plot_acts.arg_en: Price's signature chapter — the imperial cult as provincial elite self-fashioning, not top-down imposition. The book's densest methodology: empire from conquest to complicity.

brief.main: Price 的招牌 —— 皇帝崇拜作为行省精英的自我塑造技术，而非中央强加。全书方法论最密的一章 —— 把罗马帝国从『征服叙事』彻底改写为『共谋叙事』。帝国之所以能跨三大洲持续三百年，不是因为军团，而是因为地方权贵自愿学习罗马。
brief.flow: 朱里亚-克劳狄王朝 (14-68) 与四帝之年 (69) → 弗拉维 (69-96)、涅尔瓦-安敦尼 (96-192)、塞维鲁 (193-235)、三世纪危机 (235-284) → 皇帝崇拜的技术细节 (sacra、flamines、neocoria) → 行省精英的罗马化 (高卢-伊比利亚-北非-叙利亚-不列颠) → 城市作为『罗马性』的技术 (forum、bath、amphitheatre、aqueduct) → 罗马法与公民权的扩展 (卡拉卡拉 212 edict) → 帝国宗教的多元共存 (密特拉、伊西斯、玛格纳·玛特) → 三世纪危机的结构成因。
brief.names: Tiberius、Caligula、Claudius、Nero、Vespasian、Titus、Domitian、Trajan、Hadrian、Antoninus Pius、Marcus Aurelius、Commodus、Septimius Severus、Caracalla、Elagabalus、Maximinus Thrax、Philip the Arab、Decius、Valerian、Gallienus、Aurelian、Diocletian
brief.sources: 塔西佗《编年史》《历史》《农业论》、小普林尼书信 (与图拉真的往来信)、苏维托尼乌斯、《奥古斯塔史》、CIL 铭文 corpus、埃及纸莎草、行省皇帝崇拜铭文、Dura-Europos 考古、Mithraeum 遗址
brief.link: 为 Ch.10 君士坦丁与基督教接管铺路 —— 皇帝崇拜的框架被基督教皇帝从内部改写。
brief.main_en: Price's signature chapter — the imperial cult as a technique of self-fashioning by provincial elites, not a top-down imposition. The most methodologically dense chapter of the book, rewriting the Roman Empire thoroughly from a 'narrative of conquest' into a 'narrative of complicity': the empire lasted three centuries across three continents not because of the legions but because local notables willingly learned to be Roman.
brief.flow_en: The Julio-Claudian dynasty (14-68) and the Year of the Four Emperors (69) → the Flavians (69-96), Nerva-Antonines (96-192), Severans (193-235), the Crisis of the Third Century (235-284) → the technical detail of the imperial cult (sacra, flamines, neokoroi) → the Romanisation of provincial elites (Gaul, Iberia, Africa, Syria, Britain) → the city as a technology of 'Romanness' (forum, bath, amphitheatre, aqueduct) → the extension of Roman law and citizenship (Caracalla's edict of 212) → the plural coexistence of imperial religion (Mithras, Isis, Magna Mater) → the structural causes of the third-century crisis.
brief.names_en: Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, Nero, Vespasian, Titus, Domitian, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius, Commodus, Septimius Severus, Caracalla, Elagabalus, Maximinus Thrax, Philip the Arab, Decius, Valerian, Gallienus, Aurelian, Diocletian
brief.sources_en: Tacitus's Annals, Histories and Agricola, the letters of Pliny the Younger (with Trajan), Suetonius, the Historia Augusta, the CIL inscription corpus, Egyptian papyri, provincial imperial-cult inscriptions, the Dura-Europos excavation, Mithraea
brief.link_en: Prepares Constantine and the Christian takeover in the closing chapter — the framework of the imperial cult rewritten from within by a Christian emperor.

plot_acts.zh: AD 284–425｜戴克里先、君士坦丁、基督教国教化；不列颠乡间别墅的基督像——奥古斯丁之《上帝之城》作为闭幕。
plot_acts.en: AD 284–425｜Diocletian, Constantine, state Christianity; the Lullingstone villa's frescoes — Augustine's City of God as curtain.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 从戴克里先到奥古斯丁 —— 古典欧洲被基督教接管。作者以 Lullingstone 别墅壁画作视觉收束 —— 不列颠行省的边缘成为整个古典遗产的载体。首尾呼应。
plot_acts.arg_en: Diocletian to Augustine — Classical Europe absorbed by Christianity. Lullingstone villa frescoes as visual close: the provincial periphery becomes the carrier of the whole classical inheritance. Book-end symmetry.

brief.main: 从戴克里先四帝共治到奥古斯丁。作者以 Lullingstone 别墅壁画 (c.350，肯特郡基督教化不列颠精英) 作为视觉收束 —— 不列颠行省的边缘成为整个古典遗产的最终载体。『古典欧洲』作为叙事被基督教接管。
brief.flow: 戴克里先四帝共治 (284-305) 与价格敕令 → 君士坦丁 (306-337) 与米尔维安桥 (312)、米兰敕令 (313)、君士坦丁堡奠基 (330) → 朱利安『背教者』的复兴尝试失败 (361-363) → 塞奥多西 (379-395) 与尼西亚信经的官方化 → 罗马城被阿拉里克洗劫 (410) 的精神冲击 → 奥古斯丁《上帝之城》(413-426) 作为对罗马陷落的神学回应 → 高卢-西班牙-北非-不列颠的行省基督教化 (Lullingstone 壁画为象征)。
brief.names: Diocletian、Maximian、Constantine I、Constantius II、Julian、Jovian、Valentinian I、Valens、Theodosius I、Arcadius、Honorius、Alaric、St Ambrose、St Jerome、St Augustine、Pelagius
brief.sources: Lactantius《迫害者之死》、Eusebius《君士坦丁传》、Ammianus Marcellinus《晚期罗马史》、奥鲁西乌斯《七卷历史》、奥古斯丁《忏悔录》《上帝之城》、Notitia Dignitatum、Lullingstone 别墅壁画、Ravenna 与 Milan 建筑遗存
brief.link: 全书收束 —— Ch.1 的斯特拉斯堡欧罗巴雕塑与 Ch.10 的 Lullingstone 基督教壁画形成 1700 年的呼应，作者用首尾对称证明『古典欧洲』是被不断重述的范畴。
brief.main_en: From the Tetrarchy of Diocletian to Augustine. The author closes visually on the Lullingstone villa fresco (c. 350, the Christianised British elite in Kent) — the province's far margin becomes the final vessel of the whole classical inheritance. 'Classical Europe' as a narrative is taken over by Christianity.
brief.flow_en: Diocletian's Tetrarchy (284-305) and the Edict on Prices → Constantine (306-337) with the Milvian Bridge (312), the Edict of Milan (313), the founding of Constantinople (330) → the failed restoration attempt of the 'Apostate' Julian (361-363) → Theodosius (379-395) and the officialising of the Nicene creed → the psychic shock of Alaric's sack of Rome (410) → Augustine's City of God (413-426) as a theological response to Rome's fall → the Christianisation of the provinces of Gaul, Spain, Africa and Britain (the Lullingstone fresco as its emblem).
brief.names_en: Diocletian, Maximian, Constantine I, Constantius II, Julian, Jovian, Valentinian I, Valens, Theodosius I, Arcadius, Honorius, Alaric, St Ambrose, St Jerome, St Augustine, Pelagius
brief.sources_en: Lactantius's On the Deaths of the Persecutors, Eusebius's Life of Constantine, Ammianus Marcellinus's Res Gestae, Orosius's Seven Books of History, Augustine's Confessions and City of God, the Notitia Dignitatum, the Lullingstone villa fresco, the surviving buildings of Ravenna and Milan
brief.link_en: The whole book closes — the Strasbourg Europa sculpture at the opening and the Lullingstone Christian fresco at the end answer each other across the centuries, the author using an opening-closing symmetry to show that 'Classical Europe' is a category ceaselessly re-told.

narrative.zh: 编年体与专题交叉：大时间线以四章划分（宫殿时代、城邦时代、帝国时代），每章内按专题（政治、文化、宗教、经济）展开。特色在于每章以一件具体文物或文本为锚点（线形文字B泥板、荷马抄本、帕特农神庙、亚历山大金币、奥古斯丁手稿），从物质证据出发引出论证。
narrative.en: Chronological with thematic cross-cuts: four major periods (Palatial, Polis, Imperial), each subdivided thematically (politics, culture, religion, economy). Signature move: each section anchored on a specific artifact/text (Linear B tablet, Homeric manuscript, Parthenon, Alexandrian coinage, Augustine codex) — arguments proceed from material evidence.

intent.reception_good_zh: 被学界誉为「以最少文字提供最多问题」的古代史导论；对「古典」概念的建构论分析尤为精彩。
intent.reception_good_en: Praised as an ancient-history primer offering 'the most questions in the fewest words'; the constructivist analysis of 'classical' is outstanding.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 批评集中于三点：其一，虽以「欧洲」为题，近东、埃及与凯尔特/日耳曼边缘仍着墨有限，被指内核实为希腊—罗马正典；其二，为统摄「从特洛伊到奥古斯丁」四千年，经济、制度与人口史被大幅压缩，物质分析让位于观念与认同史；其三，「古典是被建构的记忆」这一后设框架虽锋利，却使部分传统古典学者担忧它把古人自身的自我理解也一并解构。
intent.reception_bad_en: Criticism clusters on three points: for all its 'Europe' framing, treatment of the Near East, Egypt and the Celtic/Germanic periphery stays thin, keeping Greece-Rome as the canonical core; compressing four thousand years into one volume squeezes economic, institutional and demographic history in favour of ideas and identity; and the meta-frame that 'the classical is a constructed memory', though incisive, worries traditional classicists that it deconstructs the ancients' own self-understanding as well.
intent.syn_zh: 「古典欧洲」是被记忆建构的——Price/Thonemann 以九卷开篇完成了一个方法论宣言。
intent.syn_en: 'Classical Europe' was memory-constructed — Price/Thonemann's opening volume delivers a methodological manifesto.

craft.zh: 从物质证据（泥板、钱币、建筑）出发而非从文本出发的论证法
craft.en: Arguments anchored on material evidence (tablets, coinage, buildings) before texts

craft.zh: Price & Thonemann 采用「文本先于考古」的方法 —— 每一章从一份关键文本切入。
craft.en: Text-before-artifact method — each chapter opens with a key text.

craft.zh: 全书贯穿「欧洲 vs 亚洲」范畴的谱系学 —— 从希罗多德到 31 世纪的宗教辩论。
craft.en: Genealogy of the 'Europe vs Asia' binary from Herodotus onward.

craft.zh: 图文互证 —— 每章至少 4 幅图版，从线形文字 B 泥板到 Lullingstone 壁画。
craft.en: Text-image cross-reference: Linear B tablets to Lullingstone frescoes.

craft.zh: 接受史（Rezeptionsgeschichte）作为章节收束装置：每章末追溯该时段在后世如何被再解读、挪用与争论，使「古典的形成」与「古典的被记忆」在同一卷内并行推进。
craft.en: Reception history as a chapter-closing device: each chapter ends by tracing how the period was later re-read, appropriated and contested, running 'the making of the classical' and 'its memory' in parallel within one volume.

motifs.evid_zh: 「古典」不是发现，而是每一代人重新发明的记忆产物——从荷马到奥古斯丁。
motifs.evid_en: 'The classical' is not a discovery but a memory-product each generation reinvents — from Homer to Augustine.

motifs.evid_zh: Price 的成名主题——罗马皇帝崇拜作为行省认同的技术，贯穿第七至九章。
motifs.evid_en: Price's signature theme — the Roman imperial cult as a technique of provincial identity, running through chs. 7-9.

motifs.evid_zh: 从波斯战争到亚历山大，「欧洲 vs 亚洲」作为一个可被历史追踪的范畴被发明。
motifs.evid_en: From the Persian Wars to Alexander, 'Europe vs Asia' is invented as a historically traceable category.

motifs.evid_zh: 君士坦丁-狄奥多西-奥古斯丁的三步进程——古典宗教的终结与基督教欧洲的开端。
motifs.evid_en: The three-step process Constantine-Theodosius-Augustine — the end of classical religion and the start of Christian Europe.

excerpts.orig: In October 2005 a huge steel, bronze and glass sculpture was unveiled outside the seat of the European Parliament in Strasbourg. The sculpture, donated to the European Parliament by the town of Agios Nikolaos on Crete, depicts the mythological princess Europa, cast in bronze, riding on the back of a steel and glass bull. Once upon a time (or so the story goes), the god Zeus fell in love with a beautiful girl named Europa. In order to gain her affections, Zeus turned himself into a magnificent bull, and carried her on his back across the sea to Crete. According to some accounts, one of their three sons was a certain Minos, who became king of Crete. So the Strasbourg sculpture acts as a elegant symbol for the place of Crete in the history of Europe: since Europa later gave her name to the continent of Europe, the Minoan civilization on Crete marks the true beginning of European history.
excerpts.trans_zh: 2005 年 10 月，一尊巨大的钢、铜、玻璃雕塑在斯特拉斯堡欧洲议会总部门前揭幕 —— 它描绘了神话人物欧罗巴。
excerpts.note_zh: 以现代欧洲议会前的希腊神话雕塑开篇——「古典欧洲」是被不断重述的叙事，不是天然地理。
excerpts.note_en: Opens with a 2005 sculpture of Europa at the EU Parliament — 'Classical Europe' is an ongoing narrative, not a given geography.

excerpts.orig: In the beginning, there was Troy and the Trojan War, made famous in European history by the two epic poems ascribed to Homer, the Iliad and the Odyssey . According to these poems, the Trojan War began when Helen, wife of Menelaus, king of Sparta, was abducted by Paris, a prince of Troy. The Iliad tells the story of the anger of the Greek warrior Achilles at Troy; the Odyssey recounts the adventures of Odysseus on his way home from Troy to the island of Ithaca. We see these two epics as largely fictional stories, but these and later memories of the Trojan War were of fundamental importance within antiquity and beyond. Greeks, Romans and others found their origins in the events surrounding the Trojan War, the founding acts of European history. Before looking at the later importance of the Trojan War, we need to understand the period in which these later tales are set, the period of the palaces in Crete and mainland Greece.
excerpts.trans_zh: 起初有特洛伊与特洛伊战争，因两部归于荷马名下的史诗《伊利亚特》与《奥德赛》而在欧洲历史上闻名。
excerpts.note_zh: 以荷马对特洛伊的追想作为欧洲记忆的起点——文本先于考古，传说先于史实。
excerpts.note_en: Starts with Homer's Troy — text before archaeology, myth before history.

excerpts.orig: These snapshots of Lullingstone encapsulate the themes of this chapter: the extraordinary stability and success of Greek and Latin culture, which was still the path to success in the western parts of the Roman empire; and the relation of this culture to the newly emerging Christianity. After the emperor Constantine had converted to Christianity in AD312 Christians moved from being a persecuted group to being supported by Constantine and subsequent emperors. The issue of how far Christianity was compatible with the inherited culture of the past continued to be, and still is, contested. We shall begin by looking at how central government became highly interventionist, which brought about great changes to civic life.
excerpts.trans_zh: 四世纪中叶，英格兰肯特郡 Lullingstone 一座乡间别墅的主人决定装饰其接待室。
excerpts.note_zh: 以不列颠一隅的基督教壁画作为「古典欧洲」的收尾——帝国的边缘成为其遗产的载体。
excerpts.note_en: Ends with a Kentish villa's Christian frescoes — the empire's periphery becomes its heir.

read_through.verdict_zh: 通读十章之后，Price 与 Thonemann 真正的论旨并非「希腊罗马是什么」，而是「欧洲各世纪如何选择性继承希腊罗马」——从荷马对特洛伊的追想、亚历山大的希腊化模仿、罗马对希腊的挪用、皇帝崇拜的省际扩散，直到奥古斯丁用『上帝之城』重新消化罗马。全书以『记忆-重述』贯穿九百年，收束于 Lullingstone 壁画，即把不列颠行省作为『古典欧洲』最终载体——是全书方法上最漂亮的一次翻转。
read_through.verdict_en: Read start-to-finish, Price & Thonemann's real thesis is not 'what Greece/Rome was' but 'how successive European centuries selectively inherited them' — Homer's memory of Troy, Alexander's Hellenism, Rome's appropriation of Greece, provincial diffusion of the imperial cult, Augustine's City of God digesting Rome. Nine centuries of memory-and-retelling, ending on a Kentish villa fresco — Britain as the final carrier of 'Classical Europe' is the book's finest methodological reversal.

observations.title_zh: Ch.1 与 Ch.9 的方法对称
observations.note_zh: 第一章以荷马笔下的特洛伊开篇，第九章以 Lullingstone 的基督教壁画收尾——两端都是『后来人如何记忆更早的过去』；作者用同一方法处理青铜时代与晚期罗马，全书由此成为一部连贯的『记忆史』而非编年。
observations.note_en: Both open and close on 'how later people remembered earlier pasts' — Homer's Troy and a Kentish Christian fresco — the same method applied at Bronze Age and Late Antiquity turns the book into a memory-history, not a chronicle.

observations.title_zh: 「欧洲 vs 亚洲」范畴的三次发明
observations.note_zh: 第 5 章希波战争、第 6 章亚历山大、第 7 章布匿战争 —— 作者实际上追踪的是这个二元范畴被希腊人、马其顿人、罗马人三次重新发明的过程；这是全书最原创的隐性论证线，但在 Introduction 里只一笔带过。
observations.note_en: Chs. 5-7 quietly re-track the Greco-Persian, Alexandrine, Punic phases as three reinventions of the Europe/Asia binary — the book's most original implicit thread, only hinted at in the introduction.

observations.title_zh: 皇帝崇拜作为『省际认同技术』
observations.title_en: Imperial cult as provincial identity technology
observations.note_zh: 第 8 与第 9 章中，Price 用自己成名研究的核心命题——皇帝崇拜不是中央强加而是行省精英主动挪用——把罗马帝国从『征服叙事』改写为『共谋叙事』；这条线在通读时才充分显现。
observations.note_en: In Chs. 8-9 Price's signature thesis — the imperial cult as provincial elite self-fashioning rather than top-down imposition — rewrites the empire from conquest to complicity; visible only on a read-through.

observations.title_zh: 奥古斯丁作为全书的真正收束
observations.note_zh: 表面上第 10 章处理 284-425 的晚期罗马；实际论证是：奥古斯丁用『上帝之城』把罗马装进基督教的历史——『古典欧洲』作为叙事被基督教接管。这是全书的哲学落点，值得单独重读 Ch.10。
observations.note_en: On the surface Ch.10 is a Late Empire survey; in fact it's Augustine's City of God absorbing Rome into Christian history — the book's philosophical landing. Ch.10 rewards a second read.

full_analysis.zh: **通读后的整体判断**：Price 与 Thonemann 用 900 年篇幅完成的是一部『欧洲对希腊罗马的层累记忆』。全书最独特的贡献不是任何单章的实证发现，而是把『古典』作为一个可分析的概念处理：每一章都问『这一世纪里的哪些人、在什么情境下、以什么目的引用更早的过去』。这个方法让本书与传统希腊罗马通史（如 Boardman、Holladay、Brunt、Goldsworthy）显著区别开。第二值得注意：作者对『欧洲 vs 亚洲』二元范畴的谱系追踪 —— 从希罗多德、埃斯库罗斯、伊索克拉底、亚历山大、罗马对迦太基的定性、直到 4 世纪护教学 —— 是全书最原创的隐性主线。第三：本书 34 位图版作者几乎都在书内文字里被处理，不是附录 —— 这在同类通史里是罕见的图文互证密度。局限：作者处理 146 BC-AD 14 的罗马扩张 (Ch.7-8) 相对粗疏，与 Ch.9 的宗教-文化密度不匹配；对晚期共和国的奴隶制与家庭经济的处理也过于压缩。
full_analysis.en: **Overall verdict after a full read**: Price & Thonemann's 900 years is really a study of Europe's layered memory of Greece/Rome. The book's contribution isn't any single chapter but the treatment of 'Classical' as an analysable concept — every chapter asks who, in what context, and for what purpose is citing the earlier past. This distinguishes it from standard Greece/Rome surveys (Boardman, Holladay, Brunt, Goldsworthy). Second: the genealogy of Europe-vs-Asia from Herodotus to Augustine is the book's most original implicit thread. Third: nearly all 34 plates are worked into the text — unusual density of text-image cross-reference. Limitation: Chs.7-8 covering 146 BC - AD 14 Roman expansion are comparatively thin versus Ch.9's religious-cultural density, and the treatment of slavery and household economy in the late Republic is compressed.
